hotspots.name: Sealed Pods (Tilted)
hotspots.description: Two pods stand upright but tilted — cyan ECG readouts cycle steadily inside. Someone is still in there.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Those pods read warm-gold on the medical side and the heart-trace is still cycling. Whoever's inside is sustaining. Whether that's life or rehearsal-of-life, I genuinely cannot tell from out here.

responses.label: Who's inside?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: The manifest lines for these two are intact. I just don't trust the manifest yet. Ask me again from a room the walls don't reach into.

hotspots.name: Sealed Pods (Right Cluster)
hotspots.description: A short column of three or four standing capsules right-of-center. Status indicators are dark.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Those pods are still sealed. Their status indicators went dark when the main power failed. I... I don't want to speculate about what's inside them. Not yet.

responses.label: Speculate anyway.
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Three possibilities. They're occupied and alive — unlikely, given the power loss. They're occupied and dead — possible. They were never occupied, and someone made it look like they were. I weight the third highest. I don't like why.

hotspots.name: Cryo Terminal
hotspots.description: An arcade-style terminal on the far-left wall displaying your character data and vital statistics.
hotspots.elaraDialog: This terminal has your biometric data — your species markers, class aptitudes, everything we determined during your awakening. You can review your Citizen profile here.

hotspots.name: Diagnostics Kiosk
hotspots.description: A second arcade-style terminal directly beside the first. Status pages scroll past too fast to read.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That kiosk was the medical officer's station. It still cycles, but the data feed itself is sealed. We can mirror your Citizen profile here while we figure out what they were watching.

hotspots.name: Tome on the Pedestal
hotspots.description: An old, leather-bound volume rests open on a low pedestal between the diagnostic kiosks and the tilted pods — the Antiquarian's mark glints faintly on the cover.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Antiquarian's Library found this for you and delivered it here. I'd read it somewhere quieter than the chamber it's pointing at.

hotspots.name: Medical Bay Door
hotspots.description: A reinforced door leading to the Medical Bay. Green status light.

hotspots.name: Bridge Access
hotspots.description: A recessed bulkhead at back-center beneath the Aetheric-crown emblem. A corridor leading up to Deck 2 — the Command deck.

hotspots.name: Green Ichor Trail
hotspots.description: A trail of luminous green fluid arcs across the floor from the foreground-left, snaking toward the bridge corridor.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That isn't cryo-fluid. The spectrometry matches nothing in my registry — and the registry is comprehensive. Don't step in it, and don't let it touch the locket.

hotspots.name: Lit Candles (Left)
hotspots.description: A small flame at the left edge of the central floor seal — recently lit.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The wax is still soft. Whoever lit these was here within the hour. It wasn't me, and it wasn't you, which leaves a question I would rather not answer alone.

hotspots.name: Lit Candles (Right)
hotspots.description: A small flame at the right edge of the central floor seal — recently lit, twin to the left.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The wax is still soft. Whoever lit these was here within the hour. It wasn't me, and it wasn't you, which leaves a question I would rather not answer alone.

hotspots.name: Inception Ark Seal
hotspots.description: An eight-pointed compass star inlaid in gold across the chamber's center. The candles encircle it like wards.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The First Wave knelt here before they walked out. The seal isn't decoration — it's a binding, an oath taken in the chamber that made them. The candles say someone is still keeping the rite.

hotspots.name: Data Crystal
hotspots.description: A small glinting crystal hidden on the floor in the shadows beneath your cryo pod.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A hidden data crystal! You've certainly got a keen eye. These were used by the first wave to store personal logs. This one might contain information about what happened after they woke up.

hotspots.name: Scratched Symbol
hotspots.description: Barely visible scratch marks on the wall behind a pod.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Wait... those scratch marks. They form a symbol — the mark of the Antiquarian. But that's impossible. The Antiquarian is a myth, a figure from the deepest layers of the prophecy. Who carved this here, and when? This predates our launch.

responses.label: Who's the Antiquarian?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: A name old enough that I shouldn't be saying it. Move on. We'll come back to this when the room isn't listening.

hotspots.name: Sealed Diplomatic Pod
hotspots.description: A pod whose status indicator is cold-blue instead of warm-gold. Something is in there.

hotspots.name: Frosted Pod Glass
hotspots.description: Wipe the frost — see who's inside.

hotspots.name: Medical Chart
hotspots.description: A printed medical chart magnet-clipped to the wall.
hotspots.elaraDialog: I wonder what that is. I don't have any record of that.

hotspots.name: Cracked Control Panel
hotspots.description: The dark pod's control panel is split along a hairline seam. Sabotage?

hotspots.name: Hidden Data Slate
hotspots.description: The edge of a data-slate peeks out from under the pod.

hotspots.name: Fallen Locket
hotspots.description: Something small has fallen on the floor — a tarnished locket and a cut ID-tag cord.

hotspots.name: Your Cryo Pod
hotspots.description: Your pod. Fallen on its side, glass spider-webbed. A handprint is smeared on the inside of the glass — yours, from when you broke out.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That's your pod. AK-74-0074. You broke the seal from inside, which the engineering spec says is impossible — and yet, here we are. We need to understand how.

responses.label: How long, Elara?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Long enough that the chronometer's drift exceeds my repair budget. I won't lie to you with a number — but the dust on the floor isn't a year's worth.

responses.label: About the handprint…
responses.elaraFollowUpText: It's on the inside. Whatever woke you up, you fought your way out before it finished doing whatever it came to do. I am — cautiously — glad of that.

hotspots.name: Aetheric Crown Window
hotspots.description: A stained-glass arch dominates the back wall — a phoenix-form Aetheric Crown rendered in gold and amber light. The glass is intact; the light source behind it is not the sun.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Aetheric Crown. This window is the chamber's spine — every wake-cycle the first crew started here, and most of them started kneeling. Whatever lit it then is still lighting it now.

responses.label: What's lighting it?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Not the sun. Not the ship's reactor — I'd see the draw. The closest match in my registry is the Hellbox's lattice running in reverse. I would rather not assume it's the same source.

responses.label: Who knelt here?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: The First Wave's medics, the founding signatories, and — the disturbed dust on the chamber floor says — someone within the last week. I do not have a name for that someone yet.

hotspots.name: Medicine Cabinet
hotspots.description: Two stacked dispensary kiosks built into the far-left wall. Each port holds a row of capped vials; most are labeled, several are not.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Medical supplies. Most are standard stim-packs and neural stabilizers. But some of these vials... I don't recognize the compounds. They weren't in the original manifest.

hotspots.name: Cryo Bay Door
hotspots.description: Return to the Cryo Bay.

hotspots.name: DNA Analysis Station
hotspots.description: A floor-to-ceiling glass column on the far-right wall holds a slow-rotating holographic double helix, marker-bands lighting up in sequence as it turns.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The DNA analysis station. It maps your genetic markers against known species templates. DeMagi, Quarchon, Ne-Yon... your hybrid signature is fascinating.

hotspots.name: Emergency Safe
hotspots.description: A reinforced wall safe with Dr. Lyra Vox's nameplate. Biometric reader sabotaged by her own hand; numeric keypad still works.

hotspots.name: Observation Keycard
hotspots.description: A biometric access card labeled 'OBS-DECK'. Stored in the medical safe.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Observation Keycard! It was in the medical safe all along. The previous crew stored sensitive access cards here for security. This will unlock the Observation Deck — the crew used it to monitor deep space anomalies. Take it.

responses.label: What's on the Observation Deck?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Deep-space sensor array. The previous crew used it to watch anomalies the chart pretends aren't there. If the comms-array confirms what the deck records, we'll have a second source for the worst of what we suspect.

hotspots.name: The Silence's Vacated Body (Catalog)
hotspots.description: A drawer in the body-catalog indexed to the Resurrectionist's Samsara-machine taxonomy — the Silence's body, tagged 'available' at the moment of her going.

hotspots.name: Unlabeled Vial
hotspots.description: A tiny vial of shimmering black liquid hidden behind the cabinet.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That vial... the liquid inside is moving on its own. The molecular structure doesn't match anything in my database. It's not from any known universe. The label has been torn off, but there's a serial number: VE-001. 'VE' — Void Essence? This shouldn't exist on this ship.

hotspots.name: Medical Log
hotspots.description: A data pad rests on the left-side workbench, screen still faintly lit.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The last medical officer's log. Dated... I can't read the timestamp. But the entries describe patients with unusual symptoms. Nightmares. Voices. Something about 'the signal.'

responses.label: Read it here first.
responses.elaraFollowUpText: The final entry is one line. 'The signal is in the room.' No timestamp, no signature, no follow-up. Whoever wrote it didn't get a chance to write a second sentence.

responses.label: What signal?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: I don't know yet. The med-officer treated it as a known referent — no definition, no context. That tells me everyone here already knew what it was. Which tells me we should be more careful than we are.

hotspots.name: Medical Log (Read)
hotspots.description: Read the data pad's final entry under the magnifier — patients across wake-cycles, the same dream, the word 'signal'.

hotspots.name: Bio-Bed Autopsy Console
hotspots.description: A small subsystem of the bio-bed dedicated to forensic readouts. Slot for an external data-slate.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The autopsy console can read external data-slates. If you have the fragment from the dead pod, slot it in.

responses.label: What's it going to tell us?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: If the slate's intact enough — a name. A timestamp of death. And whatever the dead Potential was trying to send before they didn't make it.

hotspots.name: Empire — Zero-Casualty Defender Record
hotspots.description: On the casualty-archive console: zero combatants killed, zero souls breached across the seven-dimensions siege. One combatant redirected to the Advocate's 'permanent care.' The substrate cost was levied on her alone.

hotspots.name: Akai Shi — Virus-Consumption Telemetry
hotspots.description: On the neural-archive console: post-mortem readings show Akai Shi's consumption-curve as a gradient, not a cliff. She held the Virus inside her body longer than anyone in canonical record.

hotspots.name: Medical Bay Floor Seal
hotspots.description: Concentric rings inlaid in pale stone span the chamber floor — a calibration mandala the first medics used to align the bio-bed's resonance.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The calibration mandala. The bio-bed's resonance is tuned against these rings; if the rings drift, the readouts drift with them. The lines look intact to me, but I'm reading slight distortion at the outer band. Worth checking when we have a free hand.

responses.label: Walk the outer band now.
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Hairline crack — west arc. Small enough that the bio-bed compensates; large enough that the mandala isn't a perfect circle anymore. Whatever fractured it hit hard enough to crack inlaid stone and leave no visible debris.

hotspots.name: Bio-Bed Scanner
hotspots.description: A pedestal-mounted exam bed in the chamber's center. Holographic readouts ghost above the headrest in pale cyan.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The bio-bed can give you a full diagnostic. Your stats, your Dream resonance levels, your cellular integrity. Step on and I'll run a scan.

hotspots.name: Bio-Bed Trace Marker
hotspots.description: A faint trace marker on the bio-bed's diagnostic strip — your DNA's signature, registered without your having sat down.

hotspots.name: Unkempt Neural Device
hotspots.description: A hidden device behind the bio-bed's maintenance panel. Cables still warm. A humming needle-port waits for a DNA sample.
hotspots.elaraDialog: [STATIC BURST] It's humming at a frequency your teeth can feel. A neural-bridge apparatus — military grade, built by Dr. Lyra Vox to move consciousness between a body and the Ark itself. It wants a sample. You don't know what it will give you back.

hotspots.name: Neural Bridge (Read)
hotspots.description: Lyra's etched plate beside the needle-port: 'L. Vox.' She built the bridge to move consciousness between a body and the Ark.

hotspots.name: Hellbox Lattice
hotspots.description: A free-standing imaging tower beside the bio-bed — gold pillar, cyan crown. The neural-lattice kernel that opens a portal into the Matrix of Dreams.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Hellbox. The cloning-pod's neural lattice opens straight into the Matrix of Dreams. Every descent is a small Blood-Weave bargain — the Advocate's path in miniature.

responses.label: What's the bargain?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Every Hellbox descent siphons a thread of vitality the Advocate harvests on the other side. Small enough that one descent is cheap; large enough that a hundred descents are not. The math is honest; the framing is not.

responses.label: Descend now.
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Then I'll log your re-entry vector before you go. If the Matrix decides to keep you, I want a thread to pull on.

hotspots.name: Broker's Quantum Body Scan
hotspots.description: On the quantum-imaging suite: the Broker of Nilmorg's volunteered scan. An age incompatible with a single spine; a Year-One cellular rest-mark; a continuity with one discontinuity.

hotspots.name: The Source (Echo)
hotspots.description: The bio-bed monitors flicker in unison. A face — or the suggestion of one — resolves on the central display. Patient Zero is awake.

hotspots.name: Tactical Display
hotspots.description: A massive corkboard on the right wall, layered with photographs and red string — the living web of intelligence the first crew began to assemble.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Conspiracy Board. Every entity, every faction, every connection we've mapped in the Dischordian Saga. It's a web of alliances, betrayals, and secrets. The more you explore, the more connections you'll uncover.

hotspots.name: War Map
hotspots.description: The lower section of the Conspiracy Board — pinned faction territories and conflict zones, threaded together in red.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The War Map. Faction territories, conflict zones, and strategic objectives are all tracked here. When faction wars erupt, this is where commanders plan their campaigns.

hotspots.name: Timeline Projector
hotspots.description: A floating cyan banner-scroll near the top-right ceiling — a holographic timeline of the Ages of the Dischordian Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Timeline Projector. It maps the entire history of the Dischordian Saga across the Ages — from the Age of Privacy through the Fall of Reality and beyond. Each era tells a different chapter of the story.

hotspots.name: Guild Registry
hotspots.description: The middle terminal in the far-left Architect-channel column. A console for managing guild operations and alliances.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Guild Registry. Form alliances with other Potentials, coordinate operations, and compete for dominance. Guilds that work together can tackle challenges no individual could face alone.

hotspots.name: Sealed Memory Board
hotspots.description: The bottom terminal in the far-left Architect-channel column. The Editor sealed memories out of the record; this terminal queues the sealed boards.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Not the open Conspiracy Board — the sealed ones. The Editor redacted seven memories out of the saga's record. Each board you solve un-redacts a cutscene and a Soul Stone.

hotspots.name: Captain's Chair
hotspots.description: The command chair sits empty on the raised central dais, facing the viewport. A personal data pad is wedged in the armrest.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Captain's chair. Dr. Lyra Vox designed the neural nanobot network that runs every system on this ship. She was the last to sit here before ordering the emergency cryo protocol. Something about her doesn't add up — a neuropsychologist with that level of access to the ship's core systems. Her personal log might still be in the armrest terminal.

responses.label: Who is Dr. Vox?
responses.elaraFollowUpText: Designation: Chief Neuropsychologist. Access pattern: command-tier. The trail you'll follow ends in her quarters — when we get there. Walk carefully.

hotspots.name: Navigation Console
hotspots.description: A foreground holographic console at left-center. A green-cyan star-map orb hovers above its base. An alien glyph interface awaits calibration.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The navigation console. It controls the Ark's fast-travel system, but the interface uses alien glyph sequences for authentication. Match the symbol pattern to bring the navigation grid online — then you can jump to any room you've already discovered.

hotspots.name: Diplomacy Table
hotspots.description: An eight-pointed compass star inlaid in the chamber floor — the round table where holographic faction representatives convene.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Diplomacy Table. Negotiate with factions, forge alliances, or declare rivalries. Every diplomatic decision shifts the balance of power across the Saga. Choose your allies carefully.

hotspots.name: Mission Board
hotspots.description: A small holographic strategy table beside the dais — chess-like pieces represent active operations and quest objectives.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Mission Board. Active operations and quest objectives are tracked here. Complete missions to earn rewards, uncover lore, and advance the story. Some missions are time-sensitive — the Saga doesn't wait for anyone.

hotspots.name: Cryo Bay Stairs
hotspots.description: An arched left-wall door with a blue keypad. Stairs leading down to Deck 1.

hotspots.name: Archives Access
hotspots.description: A secured passage leading to the Archives.

hotspots.name: Comms Array Corridor
hotspots.description: A corridor leading to the Communications Array.

hotspots.name: Indigo Marginalia
hotspots.description: Faint indigo annotations float at three of the Conspiracy Board's nodes — marginalia in someone else's hand, timestamped to your current shift.

hotspots.name: Architect — Apprentice Oath Acknowledgment
hotspots.description: On the Nilmorg Architect-channel: 'noted. the post is recognised. the post was always recognised.' The Console did not need a vote.

hotspots.name: Council Ratification — Inheritance Protocol
hotspots.description: On the Council-vote terminal: ratified unanimously, with one abstention — the seventh founding Watcher's empty seat.

hotspots.name: Architect's Recovery Response
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: 'Do you wish to know.' An invitation, not an interrogation. The Console does not answer the inverse — what knowing costs.

hotspots.name: Architect Record Correction — Seventh's No
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel: the eighth-epoch record correction — 'the seventh founding watcher did not consent to the fourth-epoch scrub. the record is corrected.'

hotspots.name: Architect Closing — Eight Signatures Legible
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite Architect-channel: 'the founding now has eight signatures legible. the silence remains. the architect notes the correction with thanks.' Third use of 'thanks' in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Architect — Trap-Acknowledgment
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: 'noted. the clauses are void. the trap was an honest one. the architect thanks the writer.' Fourth use of 'thanks' in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Dean's Silence on the Bridge
hotspots.description: On the command-deck pedestal: the Dean's hand resting on the apprentice-protection-protocol document. Ratified, sealed, untouched since.

hotspots.name: Architect Correction — Module 17
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: 'the absence of Module 17 was an honest argument that became a wrong outcome. the architect will not vote on the amendment.'

hotspots.name: Architect Closing-Rite Acknowledgment
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite log: 'the architect notes the thirty-one names. the architect notes the teacher who taught anyway. the case is closed.'

hotspots.name: Architect's Silence-Break Record
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: 'six watchers have spoken to six audiences. each line is real. the seventh has not spoken. the architect will not name the seventh.'

hotspots.name: Architect — Seventh-Role Boundary
hotspots.description: Pinned to the Architect-channel: 'the role waits to be named by the Ark itself, not by the architect. the silence will continue until the ark has spoken.'

hotspots.name: Architect's Closing Thanks
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite log: 'six Watchers spoken; one silent; the architect thanks the players for asking the question they sealed.' Fifth use of 'thanks' in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Architect's Record — Tarn's Departure
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: 'noted. she may return at her own discretion.' Tarn has left the Ark; Roen knows where but will not say.

hotspots.name: Architect — Closing-Rite Marginal Note
hotspots.description: Pinned to the Architect-channel for the closing rite: 'either choice closes the case. one keeps her name; one keeps her promise. the architect will not pick.'

hotspots.name: Architect Silence — Torn Page
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: asked to identify the torn-page imprint, the Console returns 'i decline.' Second decline in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Architect's Closing — Grateful
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite Architect-channel: 'noted. the plaza was the answer. the architect is grateful.' Second use of 'grateful' in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Architect's Sealed Note on I-1
hotspots.description: On the Architect-channel terminal: the keeper's sealed note opened only when the plaza asks. 'I-1 is the imprint that began the Ark. I will not name them. The plaza may.'

hotspots.name: Conspiracy Marginalia
hotspots.description: Faint annotations along the Conspiracy Board's edge — read carefully and the editor's voice resolves.

hotspots.name: Timeline Drift
hotspots.description: The two post-launch entries on the Timeline Projector's lower edge drift one minute forward on every read.

hotspots.name: Nav Console Sequence
hotspots.description: The previous crew's last unfinished glyph entry, frozen mid-attempt.

hotspots.name: Empty Delegate Seat
hotspots.description: The chair beside the empty seat at the Diplomacy Table — pulled out by Lyra's hand, in the seconds before the cryo order.

hotspots.name: Captain's Coffee
hotspots.description: A mug, half-full, on the dais beside the captain's chair. Two and a half centuries old. The handle still points toward the chair.

hotspots.name: Captain's Master Key
hotspots.description: A heavy magnetic key hidden in a compartment beneath the captain's armrest.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Captain's Master Key! It was hidden in a compartment beneath the armrest — exactly where a commander would keep their most important tool. This key opens the Captain's Quarters, the most restricted area on the ship. Whatever secrets Dr. Lyra Vox was hiding, they're behind that door.

hotspots.name: Hidden Data Chip
hotspots.description: A micro data chip wedged into the captain's armrest.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A hidden data chip! Someone concealed this in the armrest before the ship was stolen. Let me decrypt it... 'If you're reading this, the mind swap was successful. I am not who you think I am. The Engineer lives. Find the yellow coats.' The Engineer... hiding among the Potentials? And those yellow coats — that's the Warlord's signature. This changes everything.

hotspots.name: Corrupted Star Chart
hotspots.description: A star chart with routes that weren't in the original navigation database, etched into the nav-console's orb. The coordinates pulse with a sickly amber glow.
hotspots.elaraDialog: [SIGNAL CORRUPTION] These coordinates... they weren't programmed by the crew. The Warlord, through Dr. Vox, uploaded a secondary route map into the navigation core. The routes connect every Inception Ark in the fleet — a delivery network. When Kael stole this ship, the Warlord let him go — because Kael was already Patient Zero, infected through Project Vector. The Thought Virus was in HIM. Every Ark this ship contacted, every port it docked at, every signal it broadcast — the virus spread from Kael's infected body through the ship's systems into every network it touched. Kael thought he was escaping. He was being deployed. The Recruiter became the delivery mechanism for the very weapon he was fighting against.

hotspots.name: Elara (Holographic)
hotspots.description: Elara's holographic projection flickers beside the captain's chair. She seems to be waiting for you to address her directly.

hotspots.name: Data Banks
hotspots.description: The far-left wall is a floor-to-ceiling catalog drawer system — every drawer a tier of the Saga's record. Petabytes of data.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Petabytes of data. Ship logs, personnel records, scientific research, intercepted transmissions. Most of it is corrupted or encrypted. I'm still trying to recover what I can.

hotspots.name: The Codex
hotspots.description: Floor-to-ceiling cyan-lit bookshelves along the right wall, scaled by a rolling ladder. Ancient tomes and data crystals containing deep lore.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Codex. These are the deeper lore entries — the histories, the prophecies, the classified files. Some entries are locked until you discover enough connections to piece them together.

hotspots.name: Search Terminal
hotspots.description: A floating celestial orb on a stone pedestal at center-back — the chamber's database query interface. Speak any name, alias, or keyword and the orb scans every indexed record.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The main search terminal. Type any name, alias, or keyword and it will scan our entire database. Characters, locations, factions, songs — everything is indexed and cross-referenced.

hotspots.name: Clue Journal
hotspots.description: An open journal at the center of the reading table. Ten investigative arcs; the Two Witnesses record what you deduce.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Clue Journal. Ten arcs, the_watcher through fenra. The Two Witnesses log every reading you file — the canon is partly written by what you conclude.

hotspots.name: Bridge Door
hotspots.description: Return to the Command Bridge.

hotspots.name: Encoded Crystal
hotspots.description: A crystal pulsing with amber light, set on the reading table beside one of the brass lamps.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Another data crystal. This one has partial decryption — it seems to contain information about the Panopticon's surveillance network. The Architect's eyes were everywhere.

hotspots.name: Unmarked Tome
hotspots.description: A book with no title, sitting on an upper shelf of the right-wall stacks. The binding material is organic and warm to the touch.
hotspots.elaraDialog: This book... it's not in any catalog. The binding material is organic — it's warm, like skin. The pages contain a prophecy written in a language I can't translate, but one word repeats: 'Dischord.' And at the very end, a drawing of seven seals. The Book of Revelation speaks of seven seals. Silence in Heaven follows the opening of the seventh.

hotspots.name: Corrupted Scroll Rack
hotspots.description: The lower bay of the left-wall drawer catalog — twenty-eight scrolls behind frosted glass, each in two registers: warm-gold underlayer and a slightly out-of-register indigo overlayer.

hotspots.name: Rewritten Ledger
hotspots.description: An open ledger on the reading table — two entries scrubbed to blanks, one margin annotation surviving in your own younger hand.

hotspots.name: Indigo-Glow Lectern
hotspots.description: The orb's stone pedestal at center-back is ringed in a faint halo in the colour you cannot name. Someone is logged in right now.

hotspots.name: Unnameable-Hue Cabinet
hotspots.description: The tall glass cabinet right-of-center — a hand-stitched label dyed in an unnameable hue. One scroll inside is undyed and untouched.

hotspots.name: Charter Silt-Core Extraction
hotspots.description: The lower-deck silt-core on a brass tripod in the Foundation-tier wing — eight strata, the charter sitting in stratum six, two later burials closed over it.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Preservation-Order File
hotspots.description: Forty-three preservation orders on the standing-order vault, one identical signature across eight epochs: 'Per. M.' The inks shift; the hand does not.

hotspots.name: Empty Inheritance-Protocol Vault
hotspots.description: In the Severance-tier records: the inheritance-protocol vault, empty since the league's founding. The slot exists; the protocol does not.

hotspots.name: Forty Sealed Season Envelopes
hotspots.description: Beside the empty vault: forty sealed envelopes, one per Severance. Each contains an attendance list, a death certificate, and Vex Maestro's one-line 'inheritor accepted.' No name on any of them.

hotspots.name: Forty Envelopes — Solène's Archive
hotspots.description: In the audit-evidence drawer: forty envelopes, one per season, pulled from Solène's back-room archive. Each contract has a back. Every back has a clause.

hotspots.name: Atalin's Personnel History
hotspots.description: In the personnel-archive tier: hired two weeks before the first season, dismissed two weeks after. Cause: 'inability to satisfy the Hierarchy ledger-keeper's role concurrently.'

hotspots.name: Solven Tax Records — Epoch-Four Redaction
hotspots.description: In the tax-registry tier: three epochs of careful payments; epoch four shows the redaction — every Solven entry struck through, replaced with 'in arrears, year unknown.'

hotspots.name: Heron — Council Archivist Personnel File
hotspots.description: In the personnel-archive tier: a Council archivist named Heron — fourth-epoch, retired in the fifth, dead in the sixth. One assignment: 'tidy the founding records.' Nine years.

hotspots.name: Imprint-Keeper's Leather-Bound Log
hotspots.description: In the Memorial-tier sub-drawer: the leather-bound imprint log. The fourteen entries are the only ones with no inscribed name; each waits for a witness slot.

hotspots.name: Three Elders Who Refused — Long-Wait Register
hotspots.description: In the long-wait register: I-155, I-202, I-301 each refused to name themselves at the moment of imprinting. All three on the unwitnessed list for over a decade.

hotspots.name: Lectern Drawer — Empty (Tarn's Binder Missing)
hotspots.description: In the lost-and-found drawer: Tarn's lecture binder is missing from the lectern's drawer. Removed at second bell; not recovered at the lectern.

hotspots.name: Faculty Erasure Protocol
hotspots.description: In the meeting-minutes annex: 'Step one: omit the professor's name. Step two: invite as contributor, not faculty member. Step three: if declined, proceed.' Tarn was never invited to step two.

hotspots.name: Unsent Invitation to Tarn
hotspots.description: Beside the protocol: an unsent invitation drafted but never delivered. The Dean's signature is absent. The invitation has been sitting in the outbox for six days.

hotspots.name: Akai Shi's Body-Recovery Manifest
hotspots.description: In the Thaloria-recovery tier: collected by external agent — Resurrectionist Ne-Yon — within the same engagement cycle. Antiquarian's library entry deferred at the Resurrectionist's request.

hotspots.name: Empire of Shadows — Shelter Records
hotspots.description: In the Empire-of-Shadows tier: partial shelter-records from three Empire dimensions. Soul-names, dates, Blood-Weave binding signatures. Totals run to the millions.

hotspots.name: Documented Calm Intervals (Two)
hotspots.description: In the cosmic-weather tier: two equilibrium-crossing flatten periods. First calm — Second Fall. Second calm — Casino Heist's planning window. Each followed by the decade's peak flux.

hotspots.name: Apprentice-Failure Log
hotspots.description: In the apprentice-affairs tier: thirty-one entries. Each error shares a common shape — each apprentice mistook a Terminus formation feint for an actual approach.

hotspots.name: Dean's Nine-Year Annotation Record
hotspots.description: Beside the failure log: the Dean's prospective-faculty records — Auro's name on the list since Year 6, with the same annotation dated nine times.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Binder, Page 14 of 22
hotspots.description: In the lost-and-found drawer — the page of Tarn's lecture binder pulled from the festival hall's recycling bin. The equinox-address opening, in her own hand: 'I will not be teaching this year.'

hotspots.name: Fourteen-Imprint Unwitnessed Index
hotspots.description: In the Memorial-tier drawer: the list of fourteen imprints whose witnesses no longer live. By imprint-id only, the start of the plaza's search.

hotspots.name: Crucible Resurrection Record
hotspots.description: In the Crucible-inheritance tier: the Year 128,652 A.A. log naming Lycos preserved-and-reanimated, with the Resurrectionist's seal in the corner.

hotspots.name: Crucible Inheritance Manifest
hotspots.description: The inheritance manifest: the un-itemized line 'preserved instruments (sealed)' the Antiquarian moved into Anara without audit.

hotspots.name: Necromancer — Targets-List Dossier
hotspots.description: In the Necromancer-affairs tier: the dossier on the Architect's tenth-created Archon. The only entry on the Red Death's targets list whose date of elimination is blank.

hotspots.name: Matrix of Dreams — Energy Ledger Fragment
hotspots.description: In the Matrix-of-Dreams maintenance-era tier: the partial ledger. A sustained energy draw from an unnamed internal source, the editor's hand bracketing the 14% the imprints cannot account for.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Letter to the Dean
hotspots.description: On the classified-correspondence shelf: Tarn's sealed letter to the Dean. Explains the request to Roen, the planned silence, the Dean's choice now.

hotspots.name: Thirty-One Names Read at Rite
hotspots.description: On the rite-record shelf: the transcript of the thirty-one apprentice-failure names read aloud. Fifteen sent notes; sixteen sent silence. Both are read.

hotspots.name: Storm Case-Closure Correlation Table
hotspots.description: On the closing-record shelf: seven peak flux periods, seven calms, seven cosmic-consequential moments. The Storm's work as the chronicle's permission to be consequential.

hotspots.name: Forge-Workshop Box Ownership Log
hotspots.description: In the forge-workshop annex log: the PRELIMINARIES box logged to Atalin, ledger-keeper, Year One. One season; never replaced.

hotspots.name: Resurrection-Protocol Authoring Chain
hotspots.description: On the cult-protocols shelf: every canonical resurrection-protocol signed in the Resurrectionist's four-part cipher — Sanctuary, Red Death, Anara — firing in his hand long after his canonical vanishing.

hotspots.name: Resurrectionist Twin-Glyph Reference
hotspots.description: In the Ne-Yon-glyph reference tier: two mirrored crescents joined at a central axis. The cult reads 'death-bound'; the pre-Empire archaeology reads 'twin-bound.' Two readings; one editorial.

hotspots.name: Inventor's Casino Heist Accounting
hotspots.description: On a shelf inside the freestanding glass cabinet: the Casino Heist's post-event accounting, opening line in the Inventor's hand: 'the Storm's grace allowed the window.'

hotspots.name: The Antiquarian
hotspots.description: A figure half-out-of-time stands beside the orb, removing his goggles to look at you.

hotspots.name: Shadow Tongue (Presence)
hotspots.description: The orb pedestal's indigo halo deepens. A reflection in the cabinet glass doesn't match yours. Someone else is editing — right now.

hotspots.name: Broadcast Screen
hotspots.description: The top-left of the right-wall monitor grid — a large screen playing recorded episodes of the Dischordian Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The broadcast system. It plays the recorded history of the Dischordian Saga in episodic format. Each epoch covers a different era — from the Age of Privacy through the Fall of Reality. Watch carefully. There are clues hidden in every episode.

hotspots.name: Communication Relay
hotspots.description: The top-mid monitor — a powerful relay antenna capable of scanning for neural signatures across the fleet.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Communication Relay. I've been trying to re-establish contact with the other vessels — the ones that carried the first wave of Potentials into the void. I can scan for dormant neural signatures across the fleet. Perhaps we can identify other Potentials who survived the journey.

hotspots.name: Pirate Frequency TV
hotspots.description: The top-right monitor — a battered CRT television tuned to a frequency that shouldn't exist. The signal comes and goes. Sometimes a handsome devil speaks directly to you.
hotspots.elaraDialog: This... this isn't supposed to be here. It's tuned to a frequency outside the Ark's normal broadcast spectrum. The signal ID reads 'MEME-PRIME.' Whoever is broadcasting has been recording the entire Dischordian Saga — and narrating it with alarming personal knowledge. The episodes unlock as you progress. It calls itself 'Late Night with the Meme.' I don't trust it. But I can't stop watching either.

hotspots.name: Radio Console
hotspots.description: The back-alcove recessed window with a radio tuner picking up fragments of music from across the multiverse.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The radio picks up fragments of music transmissions. Songs from Malkia Ukweli and the Panopticon — they seem to broadcast across dimensional barriers. Each song tells part of the story.

hotspots.name: Static Screen
hotspots.description: A screen built into the left-wall gauge bank, showing nothing but static. Occasionally, shapes seem to form in the noise.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That screen has been showing static since I can remember. But sometimes... sometimes I think I see patterns in it. Faces. Words. It's probably just signal degradation. Probably.

hotspots.name: Training Console
hotspots.description: The central transmission pedestal — an interactive tutorial system explaining the lore and mechanics of the Dischordian Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Training Console. It contains interactive tutorials covering the lore, factions, game mechanics, and history of the Dischordian Saga. Essential reading for new Potentials. Even veterans might learn something new.

hotspots.name: Bridge Corridor
hotspots.description: Return to the Command Bridge.

hotspots.name: Observation Deck
hotspots.description: A passage to the Observation Deck.

hotspots.name: Voice in the Static
hotspots.description: The static on the left-wall screen has begun to organise itself — vertical bands of indigo arranging into the silhouette of a person speaking, then dissolving.

hotspots.name: Lower-Deck Bell Log — Three Pulls
hotspots.description: On the maintenance-broadcast shelf: three bell-pulls in the last century. Severance Year 3, a date no one will name, and this morning. The Antiquarian's name on the third.

hotspots.name: Auditor Klessa — Forty-Severance Witness
hotspots.description: On the witness-attendance board: she has attended every Severance since Year 1. Brings a single white candle and lights it during the spoken name.

hotspots.name: Red Death — Voice Mid-Hunt
hotspots.description: On the Matrix-residue intercept board: a field-recording from the third retreat chamber. 'I am the chronicle's correction. I do not hate. I do not pity.'

hotspots.name: Red Death — Word to the Chronicle
hotspots.description: Pinned beside: the Red Death's closing line. 'I do not know if that nod was forgiveness or recognition or the body's last grammar. I do not need to know.'

hotspots.name: The Erasure-Vote Audio
hotspots.description: On the transmission desk: forty-three minutes from the war-room's spillover recorder. Three voices, three ayes, three pauses long enough to have been refusals.

hotspots.name: The Hour Before the Vote
hotspots.description: The fifty-one minutes of room-tone the spillover recorder caught before the vote. Three faculty heads in the same room, no footsteps, no chairs, no dialogue.

hotspots.name: Silence-Break Event Log
hotspots.description: On the transmission desk: sixty-three seconds of six simultaneous voice-channels addressing six different players. The seventh channel logged as 'active signal, no carrier.'

hotspots.name: Lyra Vox's Fourteen-Minute Call
hotspots.description: On the voice-channel desk: Lyra's call from fourteen minutes before contact. 'They are asking what you would do. I think they already know. they want it from you.'

hotspots.name: Vex Maestro's Opening Line — Forty Broadcasts
hotspots.description: On the broadcast-record desk: every Severance opening since Year 1, all carrying the same line in the same cadence. 'Someone has to pick it up.' The line is older than Vex's tenure.

hotspots.name: Severance Year One Lap Record
hotspots.description: On the Year-One archive shelf: two casualties — the champion (named) and a witness who entered the lane (redacted). The only redaction in forty seasons.

hotspots.name: Vex Maestro's Confession Recording
hotspots.description: Pinned to the recent-recordings board: Vex's first-time-naming-the-recruitment confession. 'Someone has to pick it up was always literal.'

hotspots.name: First Trumpet — Twenty-Two Seconds
hotspots.description: On the upper-bands intercept board: twenty-two seconds of Idris's band-three trumpet. The post-launch content slot Phase 4 scaffolded; tonight's first sound.

hotspots.name: Meme-Show Transmission Intercept
hotspots.description: On the intercept board: Locke's adjudicar has pinned the Inventor-voiced transmission naming the Wolf as a predator wearing trust like a mask. The Antiquarian has not denied the framing.

hotspots.name: Storm — Voice-Fragment Intercept
hotspots.description: On the flux-frequency intercept board: a fragment captured during an uncorrelated calm. 'A calm is not the absence of weather. It is weather's permission for what otherwise could not be planned.'

hotspots.name: Storm — Closing-Case Transmission
hotspots.description: Pinned beside: a second fragment from the case-closure interval, signed in the Storm's flux signature. 'The case will close on the correct side of that difference.'

hotspots.name: Advocate Broadcast — Register Three
hotspots.description: On the Empire-of-Shadows transmission shelf: the Advocate's register-three liturgical broadcast. 'If a soul comes under my charter, the chronicle has accepted the soul as its own.'

hotspots.name: Advocate's Response to the Defections
hotspots.description: Pinned beside: the Advocate's register-three reply to the three-general defection. 'They walk under my charter still. I advocate for what they were when they chose.'

hotspots.name: 'Walk in Power' — Lyric Record
hotspots.description: On the album-records shelf: the canonical Silence in Heaven duet between the Advocate and the Human. The Empire's most-broadcast resistance anthem.

hotspots.name: Advocate's Current-Position Broadcast
hotspots.description: On the most-recent-broadcasts shelf: 'I have not stopped. I will not stop. I continue. The Empire continues. The walk continues.'

hotspots.name: Akai Shi's Last Recorded Words
hotspots.description: On the Thaloria-archive shelf — bot-left monitor: the helm-comm field-recording from forty-seven seconds before Jericho reached her. 'It was always going to be a mercy. We just have to live with which kind.'

hotspots.name: Mira's Dual-Thread Transmission
hotspots.description: A personal-channel buffer on the bot-left monitor — Mira Halen's letter home with a carrier clean of any duress marker, and her later answer refusing the question of which thread to cut.

hotspots.name: Shadow Tongue Signal Trace
hotspots.description: A signature buffer on the bot-mid monitor — the Shadow Tongue's operational signature, subtraction without trace across the chronicle layer.

hotspots.name: Plague Dragon Corpse Signature
hotspots.description: On the bot-mid monitor's signal-analysis read-out: the Plague Dragon's energy-trace, consistent with the Host's canonical wyrmhole technology. The Virus's path through the breach, settled.

hotspots.name: Anomalous Frequency
hotspots.description: A barely audible signal on a frequency that shouldn't exist — registering on the bot-mid monitor's edge meter.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That frequency... it's not on any standard band. The signal is repeating a pattern: three short, three long, three short. An SOS. But the origin coordinates point to a location that doesn't exist in normal space. Someone — or something — is calling for help from between dimensions. The signal is tagged with an identifier: 'MEME-PRIME.'

hotspots.name: Ocularum Relay Trace
hotspots.description: A trace buffer printed onto the right-foreground bench — identity-shift signatures the official record does not index. The Senne→Locke transition resolves here.

hotspots.name: Dead-Drop Cadence Log
hotspots.description: A cadence log on the bench's right edge — shipping traffic the antenna passively records as it crosses New Babylon. One monthly Locke-signed package repeats.

hotspots.name: The Human (Substrate)
hotspots.description: On the bot-right monitor, a silhouette resolves from the broadcast haze. Beneath the relay's hum, a second voice carries — not on any frequency the antenna is tuned to. The substrate itself is broadcasting.

hotspots.name: Crew Memorial
hotspots.description: A small framed plaque on the far-left wall, names etched in soft light. The crew who didn't make it.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A memorial for the crew members who didn't survive the journey. One thousand and forty-seven names. They gave their lives to keep the Ark running while the Potentials slept. I remember every one of them.

hotspots.name: Panoramic Viewport
hotspots.description: The vast expanse of space stretches before you through a curved glass wall — stars, a small distant planet, the chamber's only window onto the void.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Look at the stars. They're beautiful, aren't they? But they're wrong. The constellations don't match any known configuration from any of the mapped universes. Either we've traveled very, very far... or we're somewhere that shouldn't exist.

hotspots.name: Music Terminal
hotspots.description: A glowing earth-globe on a brass-rimmed table at right-foreground. The complete discography of Malkia Ukweli & the Panopticon is keyed into its base.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The complete discography. Four albums spanning the entire narrative — Dischordian Logic, The Age of Privacy, The Book of Daniel 2:47, and the upcoming Silence in Heaven. Every song is a piece of the puzzle.

hotspots.name: Bond Resonance Altar
hotspots.description: A low circular altar set into the floor's compass-star tiling — brass-rimmed, oxblood-leather kneeler.

hotspots.name: Crystal Cradle
hotspots.description: The pedestal beneath the globe-table. A brass plaque reads, in Lyra's hand: 'For the crystal that has not yet been chosen.'

hotspots.name: Comms Array
hotspots.description: Return to the Communications Array.

hotspots.name: Engineering Access
hotspots.description: A maintenance hatch leading down to Engineering.

hotspots.name: Strange Constellation
hotspots.description: A pattern of stars in the viewport's upper-left that seems to form a face.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Do you see it? That cluster of stars... if you connect them, they form a face. Not just any face — it looks like the Watcher. The all-seeing eye of the Panopticon's surveillance network. But we're light-years from Panopticon space. How can the stars themselves form his likeness? Unless... the stars were arranged. By someone with the power to move suns.

hotspots.name: Matrix Cycle-Fold Anomalies
hotspots.description: Telemetry overlaid on the viewport's left quadrant — discontinuous folds during the Red Death's hunt. Seven folds, seven retreat chambers, seven encounters. The Necromancer running into his own decisions.

hotspots.name: Five-Century Cosmic-Weather Console
hotspots.description: Telemetry overlaid on the viewport center — five centuries of slow oscillation between two equilibria, with Storm-active intervals pinned exactly to the mid-line crossings.

hotspots.name: Register of Nine Calms
hotspots.description: Pinned beside the telemetry on the viewport's right quadrant — the full register of nine documented calm intervals; each one a permission interval.

hotspots.name: Upper-Band Calibration Slip
hotspots.description: On the upper-band reference shelf, tucked between the bar's backlit bottles: a wafer of metal calibrated to the upper-band frequency, folded into the founding-Watcher's letter. Per. M. had access to the upper bands.

hotspots.name: Dreamer's Shield — Diagnostic Reading
hotspots.description: On the globe-table's cosmic-archaeology readout: the Shield's barrier does not register the Virus's signature as fully excluded; the signature reads, faintly, FROM INSIDE the protected volume. The cult calls it instrumentation error.

hotspots.name: Reactor Core
hotspots.description: The central archway holds the chamber's heart — a glowing forge fire above an anvil pedestal, fed by power conduits running into the back wall. The engineers called it the Ark's reactor.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The reactor core. It runs on a substance the engineers called 'Dream' — a crystallized form of quantum consciousness. It's the same resource that powers your abilities. The core is running at 34% capacity. We're losing power slowly.

hotspots.name: Crafting Workbench
hotspots.description: The left foreground workbench, laid out with tools for card crafting and fusion experiments.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The crafting workbench. Here you can fuse cards together to create more powerful versions. The recipes were developed by the Ark's engineers — combine the right elements and you might create something legendary.

hotspots.name: Holographic Blueprints
hotspots.description: A cyan holographic blueprint floats above a brass desk at right-center — schematics for card designs and weapon systems the engineers never finished.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Card schematics. The engineers were designing new card types before... before they stopped. Some of these designs are brilliant. Legendary-tier cards that could turn the tide of any battle.

hotspots.name: Research Station
hotspots.description: The right foreground workbench — an interactive research terminal with puzzles and experiments.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Research Station. Solve engineering puzzles and conduct experiments to unlock new card recipes and crafting techniques. The harder the puzzle, the rarer the reward.

hotspots.name: Forge Workshop
hotspots.description: A heavy blast door to the left of the central forge. Heat warnings; the air shimmers.

hotspots.name: Observation Deck
hotspots.description: Return to the Observation Deck.

hotspots.name: Armory Access
hotspots.description: A reinforced door at the right edge leading to the Armory.

hotspots.name: Healer's Host-Residue Research
hotspots.description: On engineering's medical-archive console (left workstation, top screen): the healer's preserved files. One draft entry on a Quarchon Potential, edited fourteen times across the week she disappeared.

hotspots.name: Anara Architectural Schematic
hotspots.description: On the containment-systems console (left workstation, lower screen): Anara's schematics expose the single design assumption — outside is threat, inside is family. The family has eaten the chronicler.

hotspots.name: Etched Formula
hotspots.description: A mathematical formula scratched into the reactor housing above the forge.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Someone etched a formula into the reactor housing. It's a dimensional resonance equation — the kind used to calculate jumps between parallel universes. But there's an extra variable I've never seen: Ψ-null. The null consciousness coefficient. This formula could theoretically open a door to... nowhere. The space between spaces. Where the Source dwells.

hotspots.name: Bench Tool Layout
hotspots.description: The tools on the left workbench, set up for a fusion job that was never started. Worn to a left-handed engineer's thumb.

hotspots.name: Ark Instruction Manual
hotspots.description: A thick paper manual on the left workbench. Cracked spine, hand-stamped dedications.
hotspots.elaraDialog: INCEPTION ARK 1047 — QUICK START GUIDE. Page 1: Step 1, Don't let it get stolen. The author had a sense of humour and a complete absence of optimism.

hotspots.name: Reactor Schematic Pad
hotspots.description: An unrolled blueprint on the left workbench. The lines are double-registered — warm-gold underneath, indigo on top, with three connection points subtly redirected.

hotspots.name: Kell's Residue Bench
hotspots.description: A side bench kept unmoved for centuries — Marion Kell's old workbench. The grain, the mug-rings, the undusted rectangle the Shadow Tongue never touched.

hotspots.name: Bio-Scanner Anomaly
hotspots.description: The bio-scanner panel on the right-wall workstation flickers with an unidentified neural signature embedded in the bulkhead plating behind it.
hotspots.elaraDialog: [SIGNAL DISTORTION] The bio-scanners are detecting... no. That can't be right. There's a neural signature embedded in the bulkhead plating itself. Not organic, not synthetic — something in between. The Warlord's consciousness was so powerful that it left an imprint on the ship's physical structure. Dr. Lyra Vox commanded this vessel while the Warlord used her as a host body. The walls literally remember their master. {playerName}, this ship has a darker history than I initially disclosed. The Warlord didn't just pass through here — this was a command vessel.

hotspots.name: Prismatic Forge
hotspots.description: The main crafting station — stone-and-brass furnace with the forge fire chamber glowing orange. Step up to the bellows to begin a craft.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Prismatic Forge. Its flames change color based on the materials you feed it — blue for void metal, green for crystal shards, gold for legendary essence. Step up to the forge and I'll guide you through the crafting process. Every item you create here provides real combat advantages in the Arena, strategic bonuses in Card Battles, and trade benefits in the Empire.

hotspots.name: Material Vault
hotspots.description: The far-left wall is a stacked storage system: a round rack of rolled scrolls + a dark cabinet behind. Secured storage for crafting materials, organised by source and rarity.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Material Vault. Your crafting materials are stored here — battle shards from Arena victories, trade metals from the Empire, card essence from sacrificed cards, and ark fragments from exploration. The vault automatically sorts by rarity. I'd recommend stockpiling before attempting any epic-tier recipes.

hotspots.name: Recipe Archive
hotspots.description: The tool wall right of the forge — hammers, tongs, and rolled schematic panels mounted in brass brackets. Every known crafting recipe is catalogued here.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Recipe Archive. Every known crafting recipe is catalogued here — weapons, armor, potions, ship upgrades, and card enhancements. Some recipes are locked behind skill levels. The more you craft in a discipline, the more advanced recipes become available. Master all five disciplines and you'll unlock the legendary-tier recipes.

hotspots.name: Skill Totems
hotspots.description: The tall carved brass throne at the right wall — five totem-medallions worked into the headrest and arms, one for each crafting discipline. Touch one to see your progress.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Skill Totems — one for each crafting discipline. Weaponsmithing, Armorsmithing, Enchanting, Alchemy, and Engineering. They glow brighter as your skill increases. Touch one to see your progress. The engineers who built this place believed that mastery of all five disciplines was the key to creating the ultimate weapon — one that could end the war between the Architect and the Source.

hotspots.name: Return to Engineering
hotspots.description: The blast door back to the Engineering Bay — walk out through the foreground.

hotspots.name: Anvil
hotspots.description: The anvil at the foot of the forge — centuries-old hardened brass on a steel base. The face is dished from a working life longer than most stars.

hotspots.name: Schema Rack
hotspots.description: Rolled diagrams in the far-left scroll rack — weapon designs, armour patterns, prosthetic schematics. Most in Lyra's hand. A few in another.

hotspots.name: Kiln
hotspots.description: The quenching pool in the left foreground — brass-bound clay rim around a hot bath. Cold now, but the chimney smells faintly of bay leaf.

hotspots.name: Auro's Twelve-Apprentice Notebook
hotspots.description: A small leather notebook hanging from a peg on the cabinet beside the scroll rack. Twelve names, forty-three waves held without further loss, nine years of work the Academy never paid for.

hotspots.name: Auro's Side-Room (Sub-Corridor Seven)
hotspots.description: The cabinet's interior panel — whiteboard, three chairs, a one-to-forty Terminus diorama. Where Auro teaches the module the Academy refuses to.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Letter to the Case
hotspots.description: On the recipe-archive tool wall: a sealed letter Tarn left behind, addressed 'whoever finds this case' — naming the case as the reader's.

hotspots.name: Blood Weave Partial Specification
hotspots.description: On the recipe-archive tool wall: the partial spec from Zyr'Koth's research archive. Multi-layer fabric, weaver-substrate intake, defensive-chain output; no regeneration; every binding consumes the weaver.

hotspots.name: PRELIMINARIES Box — Blank-Backed Pages
hotspots.description: On a low shelf inside the material-vault cabinet: forty unsigned blank-backed contract pages in a box labelled 'PRELIMINARIES.' Different paper-stock from the fronts.

hotspots.name: Solven Workshop — Sector 8 Corridor 3
hotspots.description: On the throne's right-arm plaque: the Solven workshop record — empty but maintained, 'Open by appointment.' The appointment book is full, every entry signed by the same archivist who keeps the tax registry.

hotspots.name: House Othisen — Small-Engine Assemblers
hotspots.description: On the throne's left-arm plaque: House Othisen's assembly record — Trade Empire circuit-racer components for three epochs without recognition. Their charter clause was the longest of the four; the erasure was the cleanest.

hotspots.name: Weapon Rack
hotspots.description: A free-standing glass display case in the left-center holds high-grade weapons, with a wall-mounted rifle rack behind it. Most are locked behind security glass.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The weapon racks. Plasma swords, energy shields, cloaking devices... most are locked behind security glass. You'll need to prove yourself in combat before I can authorize access to the heavier ordnance.

hotspots.name: Combat Arena
hotspots.description: The raised circular armor dais at chamber center, ringed by a purple-glow aura. A holographic combat simulation arena for training.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The combat arena. Step inside and I'll generate holographic opponents based on known entities from the Dischordian Saga. It's the safest way to test your abilities... relatively safe.

hotspots.name: Knowledge Terminal
hotspots.description: The far-left corkboard of pinned mission cards — a terminal disguised as a duty board that tests your knowledge of the Dischordian lore.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Knowledge Terminal. It tests your understanding of the Dischordian Saga. Answer correctly and you'll earn rewards. Get them wrong and... well, there are no penalties. But I'll be disappointed.

hotspots.name: Card Battle Station
hotspots.description: The left half of the right-side tool workbench — a tactical display surface for card game warfare.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The card battle station. Here you can engage in strategic card warfare — deploying your deck against AI opponents or other Potentials. Every victory earns you rewards and moves you closer to understanding the true nature of the conflict.

hotspots.name: Strategy Table
hotspots.description: The right half of the right-side tool workbench — an ornate chess board with holographic pieces depicting Dischordian characters.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Strategy Table. A chess variant using characters from the Dischordian Saga as pieces. Each character has unique abilities that modify the classic rules. It's not just a game — it's a test of tactical thinking. The AI opponent adapts to your skill level.

hotspots.name: Spectator Screen
hotspots.description: The front edge of the right-side workbench — a wide screen showing live battles between other Potentials.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Spectator Screen. Watch live battles between other Potentials. Study their strategies, learn from their mistakes, and prepare for your own encounters.

hotspots.name: Engineering Bay
hotspots.description: The back archway above the dais — return to Engineering.

hotspots.name: Cargo Hold
hotspots.description: Stairs leading down to the Cargo Hold.

hotspots.name: Fallen Dog Tag
hotspots.description: A military dog tag wedged between the floor plates at the base of the dais.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A dog tag. Name: CLASSIFIED. Rank: Assassin, First Class. Unit: Insurgency Special Operations. Callsign: 'Agent Zero.' But wait — the biometric data on the tag doesn't match Agent Zero's profile. It matches... the Engineer. The mind swap. The Engineer is walking around in Agent Zero's body, hiding among the Potentials. On THIS ship.

hotspots.name: Motivational Poster
hotspots.description: Pinned to the top corner of the left-wall corkboard — a faded poster showing a sunset with the text 'HANG IN THERE!' Signed in the corner: Iron Lion.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Iron Lion's poster. He printed thousands of these. Most of them are gone. This one isn't. There is a cat in the bottom corner that I did not, until today, register.

hotspots.name: Agent Zero
hotspots.description: A figure leaning against the wall-mounted rifle rack. Insurgency uniform, dog-tag at the throat, eyes that have already counted every exit.

hotspots.name: Trade Empire Terminal
hotspots.description: The raised central dais with a mannequin standing in the middle of a flag-ring — the main terminal for the interstellar trade simulation.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Trade Empire. An interstellar trade simulation based on the actual trade routes of the Dischordian universe. Buy low, sell high, avoid pirates, and build your trading empire. The credits you earn here are real — they can be spent in the store.

hotspots.name: Requisitions Counter
hotspots.description: The red-curtained trading alcove right-of-center — a trading post where you can buy items with Dream tokens and credits.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Requisitions Counter. You can spend your Dream tokens and credits here on upgrades, card packs, cosmetics, and more. Some items are only available through the store.

hotspots.name: Marketplace Board
hotspots.description: The ring of small flags above the central dais — a bustling exchange board showing buy and sell orders from Potentials across the Ark.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Marketplace. A peer-to-peer exchange where Potentials trade cards, materials, and equipment. Prices fluctuate based on supply and demand. A shrewd trader can make a fortune here.

hotspots.name: Personal Locker
hotspots.description: The left-wall recessed display cases — your secured locker containing collected items and equipment.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Your personal inventory locker. Everything you've collected — weapons, armor, materials, consumables, and artifacts — is stored here. Organize your gear before heading into battle.

hotspots.name: Fleet Docking Bay
hotspots.description: The right-wall recessed display cases — a viewport showing the Ark's auxiliary fleet of smaller vessels.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Fleet Docking Bay. Your auxiliary vessels are moored here — scout ships, cargo haulers, and combat frigates. Manage your fleet to expand your reach across the trade routes and war zones of the Saga.

hotspots.name: Sealed Crate
hotspots.description: The stack of blue brass-cornered crates at left-center. The largest crate has claw marks on it — something was trying to get in... or out.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That crate... the claw marks are on the inside. Something was sealed in there and tried to get out. The manifest says it contained 'biological samples from Sector 7.' I've locked it down. Don't touch it.

hotspots.name: Armory Stairs
hotspots.description: Stairs leading up to the Armory.

hotspots.name: Captain's Quarters
hotspots.description: A restricted access corridor to the Captain's Quarters.

hotspots.name: Inception Ark Passenger Manifest (Redacted)
hotspots.description: On the top crate's lid: the passenger-records page — seven names visible; eighth name redacted to a black bar of structural length. Not a casual erasure; a positioned occupant.

hotspots.name: House Marek — Toolmakers' Workshops
hotspots.description: On a side-crate stencilled 'HOUSE MAREK': three families, one tool-room, four epochs of continuous output. Same scrubber's hand on the charter-signature erasure.

hotspots.name: The Cursed-Forest Depot Placard
hotspots.description: A captured Hierarchy operations placard wired to the central crate — Fenra's domain filed not as a battlefield but as a logistics hub, the throughput corrupted souls, the depot dying under its own load.

hotspots.name: Rubber Chicken
hotspots.description: Hanging from the edge of the small foreground table with the glowing blue orb: a rubber chicken with a pulley in the middle. Why is this on a spaceship?
hotspots.elaraDialog: It's a rubber chicken with a pulley in the middle. I have no tactical assessment. I've failed you as an AI. Also — it has been here longer than any human I have ever known. Take that how you want.

hotspots.name: Torn Manifest Page
hotspots.description: A torn page from the original cargo manifest, half-hidden beneath the central floor compass-star.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A torn manifest page. Most of it is redacted, but one entry is legible: 'Container 7-Omega: BIOLOGICAL — Clone Template, Oracle-class. STATUS: Active. HANDLER: The Collector.' A clone template of the Oracle... on our ship. The False Prophet was made from an Oracle clone. Is there another one here? Is it awake?

hotspots.name: Trophy Wall
hotspots.description: The left-wall framed-portrait gallery — a holographic display showing your achievements and collected trophies.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Trophy Wall. Every achievement you've earned, every milestone you've reached. Dr. Vox designed this display system — she believed in cataloging everything. Obsessively. Now I wonder if that obsession was hers... or the Warlord's.

hotspots.name: Strategic Table
hotspots.description: The glass coffee table at the center of the chair circle — a large surface with holographic card projections for deck building.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Strategic Table. Dr. Vox used this to plan... well, officially it was 'neural network deployment patterns.' But the formations look military. She designed the nanobot operating system that runs every Ark — and the patterns suggest she knew exactly what those nanobots could really do. Now you can use it to build and refine your card decks. A well-built deck is the difference between victory and oblivion.

hotspots.name: Companion Quarters
hotspots.description: The single bed/cot at left foreground — a cozy alcove with personal effects. Elara's space and room for another companion.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Companion Quarters. This is where your companions rest between missions. Each companion has unique abilities and synergies with your build. Strengthen your bond and they'll fight harder for you.

hotspots.name: Season Terminal
hotspots.description: The captain's desk monitor — a terminal displaying the current season's challenges and reward tracks.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Season Terminal. Each season brings new challenges, exclusive rewards, and limited-time content. Progress through the reward track to earn unique cosmetics, cards, and materials.

hotspots.name: Morality Compass
hotspots.description: The cyan-glowing compass-star inlay set into the chamber floor at center-foreground — a crystalline measurement of the Ark's moral alignment.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Morality Compass. It measures the collective moral alignment of all Potentials aboard the Ark. Every choice you make — order or chaos, mercy or justice — shifts the balance. The census reveals how the community's choices are shaping the Saga.

hotspots.name: Star Viewport
hotspots.description: The cyan-glowing mirror/screen mounted on the back wall above the captain's desk — a viewport showing a nebula that seems to pulse with light.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That nebula... it wasn't there when we launched. It appeared three cycles ago and it's been growing. Sometimes I think it's watching us. That's not scientifically possible, of course. But I think it anyway.

hotspots.name: Cargo Hold
hotspots.description: Return to the Cargo Hold.

hotspots.name: Hidden Passage
hotspots.description: A shimmering doorway that wasn't there before. It pulses with purple light.

hotspots.name: Photo of a Cat
hotspots.description: A framed photo on the left portrait wall — a cat wearing tiny goggles. Label reads: 'Mr. Whiskers — Chief Science Officer.'
hotspots.elaraDialog: Mr. Whiskers. Chief Science Officer. Lyra hand-lettered the label. The cat is not looking at the camera; the cat is looking at her, who was behind it. I have been looking at this photograph for two hundred and thirty years.

hotspots.name: Cracked Mirror
hotspots.description: A small mirror tucked among the portraits, cracked in a spider-web pattern. Your reflection looks... wrong.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That mirror... look at your reflection. Do you see it? For a fraction of a second, your reflection moved differently than you did. It smiled when you didn't. The White Oracle — the face-changing guardian — was said to inhabit reflective surfaces. Some believe the Meme left the Oracle for dead and assumed his place — the shapeshifter hiding in plain sight. The universe believes the Meme was destroyed, but is it watching us through every mirror on this ship? How long has it been watching?

hotspots.name: Three Generals — Post-Defection Logs
hotspots.description: On the desk's comm-console: the three Advocate-general post-defection logs. Each general reports the recruitment as 'a relief that did not feel like betrayal.'

hotspots.name: Three Generals — Current Status
hotspots.description: Pinned beside the post-defection logs: the three generals continue under Hierarchy doctrine, still carrying Advocate-countersigned shelter. The charter is operationally enforceable across factional crossings.

hotspots.name: Locke's Correspondence Cache
hotspots.description: A flat document cache on the desk's lower drawer — every post-act letter Lyra received from Adjudicar Locke, in order. Each signed only 'L.'

hotspots.name: The Coordinator's Summons
hotspots.description: A meeting invitation on the desk, in Locke's hand, delivered by a courier on no Authority manifest. Signed, for the first time, 'The Coordinator.'

hotspots.name: The Director's Summons
hotspots.description: A second invitation beside Locke's on the desk, in a different hand — the only Hierarchy invitation that bypasses Hierarchy comms. Signed Ith'Rael, Director.

hotspots.name: Mechronis Certification File
hotspots.description: A personnel file in the desk's operational drawer — the Mechronis Academy spy-class certification whose content hollowed across nine generations.

hotspots.name: The Degen's Corner
hotspots.description: A small side-desk between the foreground bed and the chair-circle — the only piece of furniture in the captain's quarters that wasn't Lyra's. The Degen sat here on three documented evenings before her death.

hotspots.name: Vex's Workshop Diary
hotspots.description: A small book on the right bookshelf, second shelf — Vex Solène's workshop diary, the spine worn from forty years of opening.

hotspots.name: Dr. Vox's Personal Terminal
hotspots.description: A hidden terminal panel revealed behind the right bookshelf, still powered. The screen shows encrypted files.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Dr. Lyra Vox's personal terminal. Let me try to decrypt... 'Day 1,247. The Warlord's voice grows louder. I can no longer distinguish my thoughts from its commands. The Thought Virus is complete — the Warden and I have created something that will reshape consciousness itself. But I am losing myself. Today I looked in the mirror and saw the Warlord looking back. Tomorrow I will order the Recruiter's transfer to this vessel. He is already infected — Project Vector saw to that. He is Patient Zero, and he doesn't know it. When Kael steals this ship, the virus will walk aboard with him. Every system he touches will be contaminated from day one. The Source will be born from the ashes of the Recruiter's rage. And the Warlord will have won without ever raising a weapon.' She knew. She knew everything.

hotspots.name: Forced Access Panel
hotspots.description: A maintenance panel on the right wall, behind the small foreground bed — pried open with brute force. Tool marks scar the metal.
hotspots.elaraDialog: These tool marks... they're not from standard maintenance equipment. Someone forced this panel open in a hurry. The scratches are deep — desperate. Behind it is an emergency access tunnel that connects directly to the shuttle bay. This is how Kael escaped. The Recruiter turned insurgent turned prisoner. He broke out of the Panopticon, fought his way to this ship, and used this exact tunnel to reach the bridge and override the launch sequence. But look — there's no damage to the security systems. The locks were already disengaged. Dr. Lyra Vox — the Warlord — opened the doors for him. Kael's great escape was a guided tour.

hotspots.name: The Charter Fragment
hotspots.description: On the central reading table, under archival glass — a scrap of hand-cured vellum. Six legible signatures; the seventh sealed under a black blister of mineralised wax.

hotspots.name: The Advocate's Marginalia
hotspots.description: Beside the charter fragment on the reading table — a high-resolution rubbing of the charter's reverse. The Advocate's counter-signature carries the only witness annotation on the founding document.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Empty Lectern
hotspots.description: Professor Tarn's lectern at the rostrum end of the library, polished pearwood with brass piano-hinges. The binder is missing; a glass of water sits cold on the speaker's shelf.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Folded Robe
hotspots.description: Tarn's green-wool faculty robe folded twice on the lectern's bench — sleeves splayed, collar tucked. The fold she keeps on Fridays. Today is Tuesday.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Marginalia, Three Volumes
hotspots.description: Three books lifted from the shelf behind the lectern — chess primer, the Antiquarian's marginalia compendium, Roen's trial-procedure manual — each carrying Tarn's annotations down the side gutters.

hotspots.name: The Mirror Charter
hotspots.description: A second pane of glass on the reading table — the four-house delegation's mirror of the founding charter, brought in this morning. Eight signatures, not seven.

hotspots.name: The Eighth Clause Overlay
hotspots.description: A transparency overlay sliding from the catalog drawer — the mirror charter's body text laid against the founding charter's, exposing the thirty-four line clause one copy carries and the other never did.

hotspots.name: Zyr'Koth's Epoch-One Contract
hotspots.description: Spread on the reading table: the DMC season contract Zyr'Koth produced at Nilmorg's ceremony. Front in standard form; back carrying a paragraph that has been quietly enforceable for forty seasons.

hotspots.name: The Infernal Clause
hotspots.description: Under archival glass: the back-page paragraph itself. 'In the event of the champion's death, the soul-bond may be claimed by the Hierarchy in lieu of the second-cycle prize.'

hotspots.name: Your Apprentice's File
hotspots.description: The catalog's apprentice drawer — your sponsored apprentice's enrolment, transcript, and roof-assignment. Top of cohort for two terms; countersigned by the Dean and by an off-faculty instructor named Auro.

hotspots.name: Curriculum Diff — League vs Academy
hotspots.description: Two curricula on the reading table: the league's tower-defense drill curriculum beside the Academy's. The cipher-den has done the diff; one module is missing from the Academy side and only one.

hotspots.name: Auro's Module 17 Folio
hotspots.description: An eleven-page folio Sergeant Auro brought in at second bell — 'Module 17 — Feint Recognition,' written from memory and combat experience by a teacher the Academy has refused to pay.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Year-Eight Retraction
hotspots.description: The last leaf of the Antiquarian's marginalia compendium, in Tarn's hand at Year 8 — six lines retracting her Year-One curriculum argument and naming the cost. The Dean has not turned this leaf in six years.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Confirmation of the Seventh Role
hotspots.description: In the central reading dome: the Antiquarian's signed minute of the conversation with Per. M. — confirming the seventh Watcher and the Closer-of-the-charter are the same role.

hotspots.name: Forty Clauses — Contemporaneous Dates
hotspots.description: On the contract-cross-reference shelf: every clause's date matches the contract's signing week — within a seven-day window. So is every clause.

hotspots.name: Solène's Audit-Witness Recollection
hotspots.description: On the audit-witness shelf: 'the contracts came back from the season-end audit with the clauses already on them. I never saw the clauses being written.'

hotspots.name: Atalin's Current Status
