hotspots.description: On the staff-roster annex shelf: Atalin is alive. Eighty-six. Lower-deck sector eleven. Has not spoken to anyone from the league in forty seasons.

hotspots.name: Atalin's Forty-Year Account
hotspots.description: On the closer's-room recording: 'I wrote them because the Hierarchy would have written them if I refused. I wrote them with a flaw. I have been making myself easy to find for forty seasons.'

hotspots.name: Atalin at the Closing Rite
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite seating chart: Atalin sits beside Solène. They have not been in a public room in forty seasons. They cry once when the Advocate names them. They do not cry again.

hotspots.name: Solven Household Ledger
hotspots.description: On the reading-dome's delegation table: continuous Solven workshop records from founding to today. Customers the Architect has on no roster.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Closer Office — Year-Two Meeting
hotspots.description: In Per. M.'s office annex: the closer is older. The lamp still burns. The drawer is still locked. Per. M. listens for thirty-three minutes before speaking.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Silence-as-Vote Clarification
hotspots.description: Beside the meeting record: 'The seventh did not sign the scrub. The seventh has been holding the silence as a kind of vote. The Council has been counting the silence wrong.'

hotspots.name: Charter Addendum — Eight Again
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite shelf: the folio sewn to both charters. 'We eight signed; we six scrubbed; we four kept; we eight again.'

hotspots.name: Almir of the Bow — First Signature
hotspots.description: On the founding-signatures rubbing wall: Almir's signature. The first crown-bearer. Plain, almost bored — signed last because Almir was the rider.

hotspots.name: Three Sisters of House Quill
hotspots.description: Beside Almir's: sigils two, three, four. A ladder, eldest at the top; the youngest's loop runs into where the seventh signature should begin.

hotspots.name: Advocate's Marginalia — 'Six Speak'
hotspots.description: On the back of the charter, the Advocate's annotation: 'six speak; one listens; one of us is the silence.' Read correctly for the first time.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Office (Four Corridors Down)
hotspots.description: Four corridors down: door unlocked, desk occupied. The lamp has burned for twenty-two unbroken epochs — its filament mineralised the same way the wax is.

hotspots.name: Library Staff Roster — Per. M. Absent
hotspots.description: Per. M. does not appear on any roster. Key, office, desk, lamp, signature on every preservation order — but not paid, hired, or registered.

hotspots.name: Seventh-Signature Inscription Choice
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite scroll: the empty seventh signature line is open for inscription. The player chooses whether to inscribe a name or leave it blank.

hotspots.name: Broker of Nilmorg — Profile
hotspots.description: In the back-room observation alcove: the aging Broker who lives in the back rooms of the Trade Empire's Nilmorg sector. Will not give a name. Pays for the candle.

hotspots.name: Forty-One Chairs (Back Room Photograph)
hotspots.description: In the Severance-reliquary alcove: forty-one mismatched chairs, each facing a shelf at eye-height holding a glass jar with a faint blue glow.

hotspots.name: Chair One — Reserved Annotation
hotspots.description: Beside the chairs photograph: 'Chair One is reserved. I sit there each season after the bond is poured. I have not yet failed to stand.'

hotspots.name: Forty-One-Jar Inventory
hotspots.description: On the jar-inventory shelf: forty-one jars. The first jar is heaviest; its glow is steadier. The most recent jar is empty, waiting for tonight's bond.

hotspots.name: First-Chair Hidden Ledger
hotspots.description: Pulled from inside Chair One's cushion: a small ledger. Forty entries. Each a date and one word: 'stood.'

hotspots.name: Apprentice First-Refusal Record
hotspots.description: On the apprentice-choice display: 'sit if you can. don't if you can't. either way, the protocol is written tonight.'

hotspots.name: Year of the Lost — First Volume
hotspots.description: On the chronicle-shelf: hand-bound, leather-quilted, 812 pages. Seven hundred ninety-eight names inscribed; fourteen pages blank with 'unwitnessed' in pencil.

hotspots.name: Keeper's Log — Torn Page
hotspots.description: In the log fragment-drawer: the keeper's log torn at the page that should contain the fourteenth imprint's id. The tear is old; the keeper does not remember.

hotspots.name: Closing-Rite Volume — All Inscribed
hotspots.description: Beside the first volume: the volume closed at last bell. Eight hundred and twelve names — and one folio of additional inscriptions for I-1.

hotspots.name: Carrier-Choice — Volume Disposition
hotspots.description: The Antiquarian's question: 'will you leave the volume in the library, or carry it back, by hand, to the imprint room? both are honest.' The choice is the player's.

hotspots.name: Lore Faculty Proposal — Veth
hotspots.description: On the Lore-faculty submissions shelf: six modules, archive-heavy, citing Tarn's seminar series on the Antiquarian's marginalia.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Binder, Recovered
hotspots.description: On Tarn's desk: twenty-two pages, weighted by a pebble. Page one is the resignation. Page twenty-two reads: 'vote on the curriculum, not on me.'

hotspots.name: Tarn's Curriculum — Cleaned for Council
hotspots.description: Beside the binder: twenty pages copied for the Council. Tarn's authorship line is left blank by Roen. The blank is the choice the player will resolve.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Pebble
hotspots.description: On Tarn's desk under the binder: a grey, water-smoothed lower-deck stone. The pebble is heavier than it looks. The Dean has been weighing it during the vote-prep.

hotspots.name: Communiqué Appendix — Year-Two
hotspots.description: On the communiqué-appendix shelf: the Antiquarian's single-page addition to the year's Council communiqué. One year to consider what the seventh's role might be named.

hotspots.name: Memorial Plaza Volume — Seventh Appendix
hotspots.description: In the final folio: 'I will not be named until the Ark has named what I am for.' A blank page sewn beside six.

hotspots.name: Six Watcher-Lines, Inscribed
hotspots.description: On the Memorial Plaza shelf: six Watcher-role descriptions hand-copied by the Antiquarian, sewn between Aren's name and Year-3 inscriptions.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's 'Unknown' Entry
hotspots.description: On the chronicle-open-archive shelf: 'unknown — case shelved at last review.' A small later annotation in a different hand: 'kept current.' The annotator is not named.

hotspots.name: Cult-Curated Terminus Map
hotspots.description: On the chronicle-reference wall: seven walking figures around the Source Kael. Six match first-wave Potential silhouettes. The seventh wears a long-beaked mask.

hotspots.name: Jericho's Witness Page
hotspots.description: On the Thaloria-archive shelf: Jericho Jones's hour-after-mercy witness page. 'Akai Shi was already gone. I did the work she would have asked me to do.'

hotspots.name: Red Death — Open Targets List
hotspots.description: In the case-files drawer: fourteen entities the Red Death has eliminated. Each entry carries a date, a place, and the chronicler's note.

hotspots.name: Necromancer Kill — Day 15 of Fracture
hotspots.description: On the case-closure shelf: the Antiquarian's record entry for Day 15 of Fracture, Year 117,046 A.A. The kind of mercy chosen: clean.

hotspots.name: Red Death Returns from the Matrix
hotspots.description: Beside the kill record: twelve cycles after the kill, the Red Death exits the Matrix through the same fold. Unchanged. Time-displacement band intact. Targets list now closed.

hotspots.name: Case File Closes
hotspots.description: The Antiquarian's closing seal: 'The case being closed does not mean the case-bearer is.' The arc the Resurrectionist authored is complete.

hotspots.name: Closing 'Walk in Power' Broadcast
hotspots.description: In the case-closure playback alcove: the duet's final cadence, captured live from a current Empire-of-Shadows transmission tower. The Antiquarian's canonical closure for the arc.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Journal Entry XXXVIII
hotspots.description: On the chronicle-current shelf: 'Anara. My creation. My refuge. My failure.' The Antiquarian's hand-written admission of his pocket-universe's design flaw.

hotspots.name: Wolf's Predator-Ledger
hotspots.description: In the Anara-affairs drawer: the Quarchon-hand ledger matching Lycos's archived sample. Four entries, three 'mercy: n', one 'mercy: y'.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Design-Failure Admission
hotspots.description: On the Anara design-failure shelf: the Antiquarian's pressed admission of moving heroes into Anara without verifying the Wolf's containment.

hotspots.name: Wolf's First Words (Reanimation)
hotspots.description: In the cosmic-archaeology audio drawer: the Wolf's first words at reanimation. 'I will give the chronicle the kind of mercy I was given: clean.'

hotspots.name: Wolf's Current Position (Hall of Disappearances)
hotspots.description: On the Anara live-tracking board: the Wolf in the Hall of Disappearances for three cycles. Three more heroes scheduled to enter.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Closing Concession
hotspots.description: On the case-closure shelf: 'I cannot ask the chronicle's reader to resolve what I designed wrong. I can only ask: walk into the Hall.'

hotspots.name: Hall of Disappearances — Diagram
hotspots.description: On the threshold-record shelf: a circular chamber with twelve niches, each holding an empty pedestal. The chamber's ceremonial geometry annotated.

hotspots.name: Storm Dossier — Operational Sentence
hotspots.description: On the right-wall upper bookshelf (cosmic-archaeology section): the Storm's dossier open at its operational sentence. Older than every active Ne-Yon.

hotspots.name: Polarity — Lyric Record
hotspots.description: On the right-wall upper bookshelf (lyric-records row): the Book of Daniel 2:47 'Polarity' record, signed in the Enigma's hand. The 12th Ne-Yon's endorsement of the Storm/Silence pairing.

hotspots.name: Dreamer's One-Word Entry on the Storm
hotspots.description: On the right-wall upper bookshelf (Dreamer-archive section): the Dreamer's library carries one entry on the Storm — 'noted.' Nothing else.

hotspots.name: Storm Dossier Status: Active
hotspots.description: On the right-wall upper bookshelf (dossier-status row): the Storm reads Active despite the Degen-bible's 'only one still awake.' A productive ambiguity the case does not resolve.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Residency Marginalia
hotspots.description: On the marginalia shelf: Tarn's Year-Two notebook annotation naming Module 17 as the module the Academy will not teach.

hotspots.name: Auro at the Closing Rite
hotspots.description: In the case-rite annex: the Antiquarian's hand-written note on Auro's attendance. She nods once when Tarn's name is read. She does not nod when the Dean apologises.

hotspots.name: Anara League-Hall Reproduction (Empty Chair)
hotspots.description: In a quiet annex off the central dome: the Antiquarian's scaled twelve-chair reproduction of Anara's League hall. One chair stands empty; the Antiquarian has annotated it 'WHO TOOK THEM.'

hotspots.name: The Cataloguer's Pattern Wall
hotspots.description: On the wall behind the reading dome: three more re-coloured chairs. Medic, signals officer, tactician, residue-specialist healer. The pattern stopped being absence the morning the healer's chair emptied.

hotspots.name: Resurrectionist's Recovery Seal
hotspots.description: On the central reading table: the Cycle Walker's wheel-and-thread seal pulled from Akai Shi's recovery manifest. The same seal appears on the Wolf's reanimation centuries later.

hotspots.name: Resurrectionist Case-File Seal
hotspots.description: In the cosmic-archaeology drawer: forty case-files, every one stamped with the same long-beaked plague-mask seal. The cult calls the seal ceremonial; the pre-Empire references catalogue it as a worn object.

hotspots.name: Pre-Empire Twin-Ne-Yon Fragment
hotspots.description: Under archival glass on the cosmic-archaeology shelf: 'the death-bound and the cycle-bound walk in pairs.' The cult reads metaphor; the pre-Empire references read literal taxonomy.

hotspots.name: Empire of Shadows Founding Charter
hotspots.description: Under archival glass: the founding charter, the Advocate's signature at the foot, six co-signatures following — five legible, the sixth self-redacted in her own hand.

hotspots.name: Humanity-Trade Operational Specification
hotspots.description: On the Empire-of-Shadows shelf: the Advocate's itemised trade spec — three components surrendered to power the Weave, charter, and the unconditional shelter. Authored by her, in register three.

hotspots.name: The Loredex
hotspots.description: The left-center lectern with open book on a brass pedestal — the Antiquarian's living chronicle, the part he lets you walk yourself.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Loredex. The Antiquarian is one of the Two Witnesses, and this is the chronicle he lets you read on your own feet. Everything you uncover is written here.

hotspots.name: The Orb of Worlds
hotspots.description: The bronze candle-lamp at the center of the reading table — a golden orb hovering above a leather glove. Inside, a miniature city glows with warm light, its tiny streets and buildings shifting as you watch.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Orb of Worlds. The Antiquarian uses it to observe every timeline simultaneously. That city inside — it's not a model. It's a real city, compressed into a pocket of folded space. Touch it and the CoNexus portal opens. You can step into any story from the Dischordian Saga and live it yourself. The AI adapts to your choices. No two journeys are ever the same.

hotspots.name: Ancient Tomes
hotspots.description: The floor-to-ceiling left-wall bookshelves — leather-bound books pulsing with faint inner light. Each spine bears a title from the Dischordian Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: These aren't ordinary books. Each one is a gateway to a CoNexus story game. The Necromancer's Lair, Awaken the Clone, Sundown Bazaar... the Antiquarian has catalogued every major event in the Saga as an interactive narrative. Pick one up and you'll be pulled into the story.

hotspots.name: Glowing Data Crystals
hotspots.description: Crystalline structures embedded in the shelves, each containing compressed narratives from different Ages.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Data crystals from every Age of the Saga. The Age of Privacy, the Age of Revelation, the Fall of Reality, the Age of Potentials. Each crystal contains thousands of branching narratives — every possible outcome of every possible choice. The Antiquarian has been collecting them for millennia.

hotspots.name: The Antiquarian's Desk
hotspots.description: An ornate desk covered in star charts, ancient manuscripts, and a leather glove that seems to move on its own.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Antiquarian's personal desk. Star charts from universes that no longer exist. Manuscripts written in languages that were never spoken by mortal tongues. And that glove — it's a neural interface, designed to connect directly with the Orb. The Antiquarian doesn't just watch the timelines. He feels them. Every joy, every sorrow, every death — he experiences it all.

hotspots.name: Living Star Map
hotspots.description: The domed ceiling displays constellations that move and shift, showing the positions of stars across multiple timelines.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The ceiling shows star maps from every major timeline in the Saga. Watch — the constellations shift as different realities branch and collapse. Each point of light is a universe. Some are thriving. Some are dying. Some have already been consumed by the Terminus Swarm. The Antiquarian watches them all.

hotspots.name: Return to Captain's Quarters
hotspots.description: The brass-framed circular door at the back of the chamber with the Antiquarian's seal — a shimmering portal back to the Ark.

hotspots.name: Hidden Prophecy
hotspots.description: A single page, glowing faintly, tucked behind a shelf. It seems to have been placed here deliberately.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A prophecy written in the Antiquarian's own hand. 'When the seventh seal breaks and silence falls upon heaven, the Orb will shatter and the stories will become real. The Potentials will face the final choice: to end the Saga or begin it anew. The Programmer dies so the Antiquarian can live. The Antiquarian lives so the stories can be told. And the stories are told so that you — yes, you, the one reading this — can choose.' He's... he's talking to us directly. He knew we would find this. He planned for everything.

hotspots.name: Card Catalogue
hotspots.description: A brass-bound card catalogue beside the desk. Pre-Ark inventory of every story the Antiquarian has ever filed.

hotspots.name: Locked Vault
hotspots.description: A small reinforced vault recessed into the bookshelf — sealed by the Antiquarian against his own future readings.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Bust
hotspots.description: A marble bust of the Antiquarian on a pedestal. Eyes inlaid with phosphor-lavender glass.

hotspots.name: Hierophant's Marginalia Stack
hotspots.description: A small stack of catalog cards in the desk's far corner, every card bearing the Hierophant's preserved marginalia.

hotspots.name: Coda's Purpose Shelf
hotspots.description: A small dedicated shelf the Antiquarian set aside for the seven inter-faction trustee bodies. The Coda's section is the largest.

hotspots.name: Velkraal's Correspondence Folio
hotspots.description: A leather folio on the desk's far-left corner. Velkraal'Sek's correspondence, posthumous letters, and the draft of his closing edit.

hotspots.name: Insurgency Witness Roster
hotspots.description: A small bound register on the Insurgency-affairs shelf. The saga's only complete acknowledged-witness list for Vex Solène's recording career.

hotspots.name: Ocularum Founding Record
hotspots.description: A bound folio on the desk's near edge, indexed under a glyph the Antiquarian files nowhere else: an eye watching an eye. The Lord Kanshi Sha record.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Redaction Ledger
hotspots.description: A thin ledger beside the founding folio — the Antiquarian's own record of what his archive does not contain, and why.

hotspots.name: The Director's Doctrine Folio
hotspots.description: A slim grey folio in the Hierarchy-affairs section — a Department of Special Projects standing instruction, signed Ith'Rael, Director.

hotspots.name: The Shadow Tongue Casebook
hotspots.description: A casebook on the editor-studies shelf — the Marion Kell editing read slowly, and the first failure in four hundred years.

hotspots.name: Thaloria's Generational Ledger
hotspots.description: A ledger on the Thaloria-affairs shelf — the Director's recovered engagement notes in his own hand. 'Tested on cohort 4. Holds.'

hotspots.name: Siege-Keep Witness Fragments
hotspots.description: A slim sheaf in the New Babylon-affairs section, indexed under the keep, not the siege — witness fragments recorded inside the inner keep after the perimeter fell.

hotspots.name: The Programmer Infiltration Dossier
hotspots.description: A dossier filed under a glyph used nowhere else here — a door with no map. The path into the besieged keep, and the hand that walked it.

hotspots.name: The Insurance Policy Design File
hotspots.description: A design file in the Authority-origin section: the Politician's own phrase for the Six Imprisoned Minds — 'her Insurance Policy.'

hotspots.name: The Two Witnesses Closing Ledger
hotspots.description: A closing ledger on the case-synthesis shelf — the whole arc assembled in one hand, written by the man it convicts.

hotspots.name: The Collector's Catalog Page
hotspots.description: A single page in a hand that grieves nothing — the Collector's. Specimen Forty-One: a discipline kept, the donor body not retained.

hotspots.name: The Collector's Redacted Anomaly
hotspots.description: An entry under the Antiquarian's own redaction-discipline — the one 'donor retained, by request,' dated the year of the Fall, the requester struck out.

hotspots.name: The Collector Case-Closing Ledger
hotspots.description: A closing ledger on the case-synthesis shelf — the Collector arc assembled in one hand, the verdict deliberately left open.

hotspots.name: The Varkul Vigil Cross-Catalogue
hotspots.description: A cross-catalogued observation under the Antiquarian's glyph for a vigil with no end — what a centuries-long unbroken post does to the one who holds it.

hotspots.name: The Varkul Testimony-Boundary File
hotspots.description: A boundary file in the Antiquarian's hand — not what Varkul said, but the precise edge of it, and the case the Two Witnesses leave open.

hotspots.name: Akai Shi's Witness Statements
hotspots.description: Akai Shi's testimony, canonized in the Two Witnesses' chronicle — the killing through the throne, and the second statement that does not retract it.

hotspots.name: The Necromancer Case-Closing Ledger
hotspots.description: A closing ledger on the case-synthesis shelf — the Necromancer arc assembled in one hand, the dual-reading closure deliberately left open.

hotspots.name: The Sisters-of-the-Weave Cross & Closing Ledger
hotspots.description: A cross-catalogue under the glyph for a record with a name struck out — three students of the Blood Weave — filed beside the Zyr'Koth case-synthesis ledger and its closing question.

hotspots.name: The Sisters-of-the-Weave Pedigree
hotspots.description: A pre-Severance Thaloria cross-reference under the glyph for a lineage with a name worn off — one lost-named instructor, three students of the Blood Weave, one struck from the Hierarchy's record.

hotspots.name: The Taskmaster's Closing Ledger
hotspots.description: A case-synthesis ledger under the glyph for a portfolio entry that never closed — the siege filed as a quarter assembled in one hand, and the genuine tri-verdict closing question the archive pre-judges none of.

hotspots.name: The Door-and-Engine Folio
hotspots.description: A cross-catalogued folio filed beside the Varkul vigil cross-catalogue — the Necromancer's two senior creations as one design, and the asymmetry that Varkul receives the maker's signal and Fenra does not.

hotspots.name: The Fenra Closing Ledger
hotspots.description: The case-synthesis ledger under the glyph for an engine that does not stop — the Fenra arc assembled in one hand, and the genuine tri-verdict closing question that closes the §XVI Mystery Engine roster, pre-judging none.

hotspots.name: Reactor Core
hotspots.description: The central-back orange-glowing reactor pylon with clock/gauge dial — a sphere of pure energy suspended by magnetic fields, pulsing with the heartbeat of the Ark.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Reactor Core. It runs on compressed dark energy harvested from collapsed dimensions. The DeMagi called it 'The Breath of Creation.' It generates enough power to fold space-time. The Architect modified it to also serve as a beacon — broadcasting across every reality simultaneously. That's how the Ark finds lost Potentials like you.

hotspots.name: Warp Drive Schematics
hotspots.description: The right-side wall panel with brass-rimmed inset — holographic blueprints showing the Ark's dimensional fold engine in extraordinary detail.
hotspots.elaraDialog: These schematics show the Ark's warp drive — but not the one in Engineering Bay. This is the real drive. It doesn't move through space. It folds space around the Ark. The Architect reverse-engineered it from Quarchon quantum tunneling technology. Only an Engineer would understand the mathematics involved.

hotspots.name: Return to Engineering Bay
hotspots.description: The right-edge sealed blast door back to the main engineering section.

hotspots.name: Reactor Coil
hotspots.description: The left-foreground workbench's brass-and-steel column running phosphor-green coolant — the hardware is nominal; the schematic is not.

hotspots.name: Coolant Pipe Array
hotspots.description: The right-foreground workbench's six coolant lines feeding the secondary loop. The pipes are correct; any future repair following the edited schematic would reroute them.

hotspots.name: Core Terminal
hotspots.description: The small left-wall console with three oxblood-leather levers — coolant flow, reactor draw, emergency shutdown. The shutdown lever is locked.

hotspots.name: Resonance Frequency
hotspots.description: A specific harmonic emanating from the foreground floor channel — the steam-vented strip seems to encode a message.
hotspots.elaraDialog: That frequency... it's not random. It's a message encoded in the core's harmonic oscillation. The Architect left it here for whoever found this room. It says: 'The machine remembers what the maker forgets. Build well, Engineer. The next Ark is yours to design.'

hotspots.name: Storm-Class Flux Signature
hotspots.description: On the left workbench (calibration-class instrument): a non-natural flux signature detectable wherever the equilibrium-crossing pattern shows. The convention names it 'Storm-class.' Nothing else does.

hotspots.name: Cosmic Energy-Balance Audit
hotspots.description: On the left workbench (Game Master's audit panel): volatility-source and fixed-archive-source instrumented against the Polarity canon, their interaction-product yielding the universe's net positive.

hotspots.name: Severance Protocol — Lineage Note
hotspots.description: On the left workbench (substrate-research panel): Zyr'Koth's lineage note — the Severance Protocol is the Blood Weave's offensive inversion. Both share the substrate-consumption signature.

hotspots.name: Resurrection-Protocol Activation Timestamp
hotspots.description: On the right workbench (substrate-timestamp bench): a protocol activation timestamped to the Plague Dragon's death-instant. The cult calls the timestamp coincidental; the Antiquarian's discipline does not.

hotspots.name: Necromancer Matrix-Escape Cipher Match
hotspots.description: Pinned beside on the right workbench: the Necromancer's Matrix-escape signature matching three of four parts of the Resurrectionist's cipher.

hotspots.name: Engineer Zero — Initialled Signature
hotspots.description: On the right workbench (founding-records bench): Engineer Zero's signature, initialled rather than written. A clean Z above a horizontal bar. The bar runs into the wax.

hotspots.name: House Vyn — Lower-Deck Hydroponic Gardens
hotspots.description: On the right workbench (lower-deck-hydroponics console): kept by Vyn descendants for four epochs. Same scrubber's hand on their tax-record erasure.

hotspots.name: Advocate Engaged — First Question
hotspots.description: In the Council-retainer chamber: the Advocate engaged within minutes of Zyr'Koth's arrival. First question: 'how many other contracts carry this clause?'

hotspots.name: Advocate's Date-Forgery Observation
hotspots.description: On the Advocate's audit-bench: 'each clause is dated to the contract's signing week. but the dates are forged.'

hotspots.name: Zyr'Koth's Formal Withdrawal
hotspots.description: On the Council-record desk: 'the claim is withdrawn. the audit was honest.' Ceremonial fee of one hundred dream tokens for the audit's costs.

hotspots.name: Bond Poured — Year Two
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite ceremonial stand: Solène pours the season's bond into the empty jar. The chair is sat in by the apprentice (or by Solène alone). The bond is calm.

hotspots.name: Kassel's Council-Chamber Speech
hotspots.description: In the Council-chamber recording: Kassel's eight-minute speech. She names Heron, the six founders, the seventh's silence as the no-vote it always was. She does not name the seventh.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's First Reading Recording
hotspots.description: On the first-bell recording: the Antiquarian read the charter aloud to an empty chamber and could not continue at the seventh signature for almost a minute. The recording survives.

hotspots.name: Per. M. Confrontation — Admissible Record
hotspots.description: On the confrontation-record shelf: Per. M.'s direct answer. 'I sealed it. I will not say more, and I will not unseal it.'

hotspots.name: Closer's Account — Thirty-Eight Minutes
hotspots.description: On the closing-day record: Per. M. speaks for thirty-eight minutes. A Watcher signed the founding charter, accepted the post of closer, sealed their own name. Both will end together.

hotspots.name: Companion on the Witness Table
hotspots.description: On the witness-table: a first-circuit eidolon ribboned with the champion's colors. Bond strength reads at peak. Looking for someone they can no longer find.

hotspots.name: Broker's Recorded Statement
hotspots.description: On the recorded-statements console: 'I picked up the first bond because no one else would. I've been picking them up because no one else has learned.'

hotspots.name: Successor-Test Recording
hotspots.description: Beside the Broker's record: 'pour the bond into the empty jar; sit in chair one; stand when you can.' If you cannot stand, Klessa pours the wax.

hotspots.name: Bond Poured at Second-to-Last Bell
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite ceremonial stand: the companion's bond decanted into the empty jar. The jar weighs slightly more than every previous jar — no one knows why. The bond is calm.

hotspots.name: Plaza Inscription Register — Opening
hotspots.description: In the plaza-register alcove: the first three inscriptions are quiet. The fourth player hesitates at the unwitnessed pages.

hotspots.name: Plaza Consensus — Twenty-Three Names for I-1
hotspots.description: In the closing-rite alcove: three minutes of silence, then twenty-three names from twenty-three players. The keeper writes them all down.

hotspots.name: Aren's Three-Hour Closing Reading
hotspots.description: On the closing-recording desk: Aren of the lower decks reads the volume aloud at last bell. Three hours. One forty-five-second pause at I-1's folio.

hotspots.name: Dean's Last-Sighting Recording
hotspots.description: In the witness chamber: the Dean saw Tarn at second bell, walking with the binder toward the festival hall. The Dean did not walk with her — the last hundred steps alone, always.

hotspots.name: Othmar's Admission
hotspots.description: On the faculty-confession board: 'I voted aye because Veth would have voted aye. I was wrong about Veth. I am not sorry I was wrong.'

hotspots.name: Roen's Admission
hotspots.description: Beside Othmar's: 'I voted aye because Othmar would. I have a private reason and I will not say it here.' Roen will say it in episode four.

hotspots.name: Veth's Admission
hotspots.description: Beside Roen's: 'I voted aye because Roen would. I have been telling myself for a week that I voted aye because the curriculum needed it. I have not been honest.'

hotspots.name: Player's Personal Watcher-Line
hotspots.description: In the personal-line alcove: the line addressed to the player, six minutes after Seal VII broke. Single sentence. Personalised to the player's saga-choices.

hotspots.name: Watcher Line-Matching Console
hotspots.description: Beside the personal-line alcove: the line-matching console runs the player's case-history against the six Watcher signatures to identify the speaker.

hotspots.name: Watcher Speaker-Assignment Resolution
hotspots.description: On the speaker-assignment console: cross-referencing the player's case-history against the six role-registry entries. The audience the player has belonged to most identifies the speaker.

hotspots.name: Dreamer's Quarantine on the Reanimation
hotspots.description: In the Ne-Yon arbitration alcove: the Dreamer's quarantine filing on the Resurrectionist's actions in the wake of Akai Shi's reanimation. Canonically open; never lifted.

hotspots.name: Apprentice After-Action Recordings
hotspots.description: In the witness chamber: three apprentices, three different years, three identical lines about reading the formation as a real approach.

hotspots.name: Auro's Statement to the Sanctum
hotspots.description: Beside the apprentice recordings: Auro's short statement. 'I teach because the apprentices need it. I do not need a chair.'

hotspots.name: Lyra Vox's Advocacy Note
hotspots.description: On the advocacy log: Lyra's decision to dedicate tonight's album track to Auro. 'I am tired of waiting for someone else to start.'

hotspots.name: Festival-Album Track 16
hotspots.description: In the playback alcove: Track 16 plays at the closing rite. 'Sergeant who taught the module the Academy would not — we hear you.'

hotspots.name: Tarn's Recorded Message
hotspots.description: In the playback alcove: the recording Tarn set to play at festival opening. The recorder failed to fire; the sanctum staff recovered it intact two evenings later.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Plaza Address
hotspots.description: In the witness chamber: the Antiquarian's first-bell address asking the gathered players to witness fourteen imprints — and the plaza's immediate, ready response.

hotspots.name: Kassel Solven's Testimony
hotspots.description: The sanctum's witness-chamber recording of Kassel Solven's eight-minute statement: four generations of waiting, a workshop kept across four epochs of administrative absence.

hotspots.name: Zyr'Koth's Concession Recording
hotspots.description: In the witness chamber: Zyr'Koth's recorded response to the Advocate's brief, read into the Council record. A long pause, then concession.

hotspots.name: CoNexus Story — 'The Ninth'
hotspots.description: In the CoNexus playback alcove: the Advocate's own narrated meditation on the ninth position. Steady register-three liturgical pace across the full duration.

hotspots.name: Probability Sphere
hotspots.description: The back-wall vaulted oculus showing the purple nebula — a window onto compressed probability fields.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Probability Sphere. It contains every possible future of the Dischordian Saga compressed into a single point. When an Oracle touches it, they can navigate the probability streams — see which choices lead to salvation and which lead to destruction. The original Oracle used this to guide the Panopticon's decisions. Now it responds to you.

hotspots.name: Meditation Platforms
hotspots.description: The floor compass rings encircling the central pool — hovering platforms that amplify precognitive abilities.
hotspots.elaraDialog: These platforms use quantum entanglement to synchronize your neural patterns with the probability field. Sit on one and your visions become clearer, more detailed. The original Oracle spent centuries here, mapping every possible future. Some say they went mad from seeing too much. Others say they achieved perfect clarity.

hotspots.name: Return to Observation Deck
hotspots.description: The shimmering portal back to the Observation Deck.

hotspots.name: Sealed Vision
hotspots.description: A sealed crystal on the side-altar — a single frozen vision the Oracle locked away.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A sealed vision. The Oracle locked this one away because it was too dangerous to share. It shows... the end. The final moment of the Saga. I can't see the details — only an Oracle can unseal it. But the emotion radiating from it is overwhelming. Hope and terror in equal measure.

hotspots.name: Oracle Pool
hotspots.description: The central glowing purple/cyan pool sunk into the floor — brass-rimmed and sigil-engraved. The water reflects something that is not in the pool.

hotspots.name: Prophecy Tablet
hotspots.description: The left-side lectern with candle — a brass-pedestal'd slate. Currently blank, but the brass beneath has been worn smooth by thousands of writings.

hotspots.name: Incense Brazier
hotspots.description: The right-side brazier with green flame on a chain, smoking phosphor-lavender. The smoke falls toward the pool rather than rising.

hotspots.name: Seer's Recording Cabinet
hotspots.description: A recessed brass-bound glass-fronted cabinet behind the brazier. Hand-typed labels on every reel-tape canister.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Pencil Reply
hotspots.description: Inside the correspondence drawer: the founding-Watcher's letter to Per. M., stapled to a three-word pencil reply. 'I will close.'

hotspots.name: The Apprentice Oath
hotspots.description: In the classified-correspondence drawer: eight hand-written lines, no signature. 'I will pour the bond and sit until I can stand.' Waiting forty seasons for a successor.

hotspots.name: Imprint I-17 — Aren of the Lower Decks
hotspots.description: On the imprint-room's cold-shelf: dish I-17 lifted to the listening cradle. Aren named themselves at the moment of imprinting; the plaza inscribes them without a second witness.

hotspots.name: Imprint-Keeper's Thirty-Year Account
hotspots.description: On the imprint-room's reading desk: the keeper's signed statement. Every imprint can be heard; the fourteen are not difficult to read, only to write.

hotspots.name: The Council's Scrub Request
hotspots.description: Inside the classified-correspondence drawer: the fourth-epoch request signed by all six legible founders. The seventh signature line is wax-eaten in the same way the charter is.

hotspots.name: Idris's Archived Role Registry
hotspots.description: Inside the role registry: Idris's archived entry — 'speaks to investigators when the investigator has earned the speaking-to.' Per. M.'s footnote on the earning.

hotspots.name: The Seventh's Unwritten Line
hotspots.description: In the classified drawer: the seventh slot. No name, no band, no audience — a single line in Per. M.'s hand: 'I will not be named until the Ark has named what I am for.'

hotspots.name: Necromancer's Last Recorded Appearance
hotspots.description: In the classified faction-witness drawer: the Necromancer at the Plague Dragon kill-site, arriving at the death-instant and departing within minutes. The cult calls it forensic; the Archon does not perform forensics.

hotspots.name: Silence's Body-Claim Record
hotspots.description: On the Ne-Yon body-claim shelf: the Silence's record. A plague-mask seal at the lower-left corner — the only Ne-Yon body-claim record in the chronicle carrying such a seal.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Sealed-Inside Drawer
hotspots.description: In the empty-drawer alcove: Per. M.'s desk drawer is sealed. The lock is the same alloy as the wax. The Advocate writes that the drawer was sealed from the inside.

hotspots.name: Forty-One Charter Drafts
hotspots.description: In the unsealed-drawer drawer: forty-one drafts of the founding charter, every one with seven signatures, every seventh sealed by wax. Per. M.'s habit is older than the charter.

hotspots.name: Drawer's Opening Question
hotspots.description: On the inside of Per. M.'s sealed drawer: 'WHO DOES NOT WISH TO BE NAMED?' Beneath, in pencil: 'I do not.'

hotspots.name: Founding-Watcher's Letter to Per. M.
hotspots.description: Among the drafts: a letter signed in the wax-thumb hand. 'You will not be named. You will not be forgotten. You will be the one who closes the seal.'

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Next-Year Recording
hotspots.description: On the long-arrangement shelf: 'whoever names me next year will be naming a Watcher who has been the silence longer than any of us has been alive. Be ready for what they say back.'

hotspots.name: Year-One Envelope (Two Pages)
hotspots.description: In the founding-records drawer: the first Severance's envelope is thicker. Page two contains a hand-drawn diagram with a fourth figure marked only by a circle and the word 'first.'

hotspots.name: Imprint Room — Fourteen Obsidian Dishes
hotspots.description: In the imprint-room alcove: fourteen obsidian dishes on a low shelf. Each dish small enough to hold in a palm. The room is cold by design.

hotspots.name: Imprint I-3 — Child's Voice
hotspots.description: Dish I-3 lifted to the cradle. A child's voice. 'Tell my mother I am here.' No name. The mother is one of the fourteen.

hotspots.name: Imprint I-44 — Forgotten Own Name
hotspots.description: Dish I-44 on the cold-shelf. 'I forgot it. I forgot my own name. Tell whoever finds me to write it for me.'

hotspots.name: Three Children Without Witnesses
hotspots.description: On the children-without-witnesses shelf: Aren self-named; the three remaining are I-44, I-244, and the torn-page child (fragment reads 'I-1').

hotspots.name: Elder's Refusal — Recorded Reason
hotspots.description: Pinned to the keeper's log: I-155's side-note. 'I am not refusing my name; I am refusing to be named in a hurry. The plaza will arrive.'

hotspots.name: I-1 Dish — Three-Year-First Listening
hotspots.description: The keeper opens the alcove. The dish is read for the first time in three years. A child's voice between three and five. 'I am here. I will be here.'

hotspots.name: Imprint I-1's Sealed Alcove Dish
hotspots.description: Smaller than the others. Older. Held in a separate alcove with its own lock. The keeper has held the key for three years and has never opened the alcove.

hotspots.name: Antiquarian's Next-Year Hook
hotspots.description: On the next-year hook shelf: 'the seventh Watcher is silent because the seventh Watcher has not yet been asked. next Memorial Day, six of the seven will speak.'

hotspots.name: Verel — Archived Role
hotspots.description: In the role-registry drawer: 'Verel of the carrying-band — speaks to caretakers when the caretaking has carried someone forward.'

hotspots.name: Kallium — Reflective-Band Role
hotspots.description: Beside Verel's entry: 'Kallium of the reflective band — speaks to combatants when the combat has cost the combatant something they did not have to spend.'

hotspots.name: Mereth — Resonant-Band Role
hotspots.description: Beside Kallium's: 'Mereth of the resonant band — speaks to musicians when the musician has heard a thing the musician was not given to hear.'

hotspots.name: Ophran — Long-Spectrum Band Role
hotspots.description: Beside Mereth's: 'Ophran of the long-spectrum band — speaks to traders when a trade has carried more than its weight.'

hotspots.name: Sothe — High-Bright-Band Role
hotspots.description: Beside Ophran's: 'Sothe of the high bright band — speaks to children when the child has named a thing the elders had not named.'

hotspots.name: Seventh Slot — Missing Archive Entry
hotspots.description: At the bottom of the role-registry drawer: the seventh slot has a number — VII — and a single line. No name. No band. No audience.

hotspots.name: Memorial Plaza Vault — Sealed Question
hotspots.description: On the Memorial Plaza vault shelf: an envelope, signed and sealed. To be opened next Memorial Day. Multiple players' questions are sealed alongside.

hotspots.name: Plague Mask at the Kill-Site
hotspots.description: Inside the recovered-artifacts drawer: a long-beaked plague mask, perfectly preserved, no occupant. Matches in every contour the seal on every Resurrectionist case-file. The cult does not connect the two.

hotspots.name: League Trust-Signature Security Logs
hotspots.description: In the League security-log drawer: no forced entries on any of the four chambers. Each hero, in their final logged moment, was either with a trusted League member or walking towards one.

hotspots.name: Silence's Information-Control Logs
hotspots.description: In the information-control tier: every classification decision is permanent, every retraction denied, every leak sealed. Silence is the locked archive.

hotspots.name: Storm Case — Silence Co-Signature
hotspots.description: On the case-closure shelf: the Silence's flat-line co-signature in the lower margin of the closing documents. She does not normally co-sign cases.

hotspots.name: The Sacrum — Sealed Reliquary
hotspots.description: In the classified-reliquary drawer: the reliquary the Advocate sealed and Syl'Vex unsealed. Weave-derivative agency-cost bindings — the doctrine the Hierarchy built recruitment-as-relief on.

hotspots.name: Contract Altar
hotspots.description: The Hierarchy answers by contract. Every summon is a clause.
hotspots.elaraDialog: A summoning altar bound to the Hierarchy's contract law. Every demon you call owes exactly what was signed — not one clause more. Mol'Garath audits the ledger quarterly.

hotspots.name: Weapon Arsenal
hotspots.description: The glowing light-coin alcoves on the side walls — small sealed cases containing legendary weapons from across the Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Agent Zero's personal collection. The Whisper Blade — kills without a sound. The Phase Pistol — shoots through walls. The Null Dart — erases memories. Each weapon was designed for a specific target. Some of those targets were gods. The fact that these weapons exist means someone, somewhere, needed to kill something that shouldn't have been killable.

hotspots.name: Infiltration Table
hotspots.description: The central blade-on-pedestal at chamber center, lit by overhead spotlight — projects a holographic table showing routes, blind spots, and vulnerabilities.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The infiltration map. It shows every security system, every patrol route, every blind spot in every major installation across the Saga. The Panopticon, the Terminus Hive, the Quarchon Quantum Citadel — all mapped in perfect detail. Agent Zero spent lifetimes gathering this intelligence. Now it's yours.

hotspots.name: Return to Armory
hotspots.description: The concealed passage back to the main Armory.

hotspots.name: Final Contract
hotspots.description: A sealed dossier marked with a skull emblem.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Agent Zero's final contract. Never completed. The target... is the Architect himself. Someone hired Zero to kill the creator of the Inception Ark. The contract was never fulfilled because Zero discovered the truth — killing the Architect would unravel every reality simultaneously. So Zero sealed the contract here as a warning: some targets must never be eliminated.

hotspots.name: Sealed Cell Glass
hotspots.description: A tall reinforced-glass cylinder full of the unnameable indigo hue, dense as water. A figure resolves only when you look at it through someone else's eyes.

hotspots.name: Manuscript Pile
hotspots.description: Stage-left pedestal stacked carelessly with leather folios — a fair copy of the editor's whole novel, kept in plain sight.

hotspots.name: Warden Terminal
hotspots.description: A stage-right brass console with a single phosphor-lavender readout — the editor's live active-edit count.

hotspots.name: Release-or-Seal Lever
hotspots.description: A long brass lever in the foreground. Three positions: SEAL, NEUTRAL, RELEASE. Currently neutral.

hotspots.name: The Unopened Threshold
hotspots.description: A door set into the vault's far wall that has never been opened — not sealed, held. The room's own commentary on a vigil that does not relent.

hotspots.name: The Maker's Heartbeat Trace
hotspots.description: A second readout on the warden-terminal no warden watches — a flat, contentless pulse the Order logs but cannot decode, because there is nothing in it to decode.

hotspots.name: The Necromancer's Altar
hotspots.description: A stained-glass altar-facet the vault renders against its far wall only when witnessed — the Cathedral of Code's altar, where Varkul speaks his four sentences and the maker's hand recently cut a correction.

hotspots.name: Holographic Battle Map
hotspots.description: The central round war-table with cosmic star-map projection, 5 faction banners standing on its edge — tracks every military asset across every timeline.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Battle Map. It tracks every military asset across every timeline. Those red markers are Terminus Swarm incursions. The blue ones are Panopticon defense fleets. The gold ones... those are unknown. Iron Lion marked them as 'Potential Forces' — armies that don't exist yet but could be raised by the right commander. That's you, Soldier.

hotspots.name: Tactical Archives
hotspots.description: The right-wall white text panel with brass frame — sealed military records from every major conflict in the Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Military records from every war in the Dischordian Saga. Battle formations, casualty reports, after-action reviews. Iron Lion studied every defeat to ensure it never happened again. The most classified file is labeled 'Operation Final Dawn' — a contingency plan for if the Terminus Swarm breaches all defenses. It requires a Soldier of exceptional courage to execute.

hotspots.name: Guild War Command
hotspots.description: The left-wall bookshelf of bound folios — a tactical console for coordinating guild war operations.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Guild War Command console. Coordinate with your guild to wage war against rival guilds. Deploy troops, capture territories, and earn glory for your alliance. The strongest guilds control the most valuable sectors of the Saga.

hotspots.name: Faction War Map
hotspots.description: Three overhead holographic UI panels (green/cyan/purple) showing faction conflict zones and territory control.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Faction War Map. The great factions of the Dischordian Saga are locked in eternal conflict. Choose your side, fight for territory, and shape the outcome of the Saga. Your faction's victories and defeats ripple across every timeline.

hotspots.name: Return to Command Bridge
hotspots.description: The reinforced corridor back to the main Bridge.

hotspots.name: Iron Lion's Medal
hotspots.description: A battered medal of valor pinned to the foreground chair.
hotspots.elaraDialog: Iron Lion's Medal of Valor. Awarded for holding the line at the Siege of the Panopticon when all seemed lost. He fought for seventy-two hours without rest, rallying broken units and turning retreat into counterattack. The medal is scratched and dented — he wore it into every battle after. He said it reminded him what he was fighting for: not victory, but the people behind him.

hotspots.name: Festival-Roof Wave Telemetry
hotspots.description: The main holo-tank's reading of the apprentice's incoming Terminus wave. Standard pattern, fourteen carriers, fully winnable — fourteen years of fully winnable waves the apprentices have failed to win.

hotspots.name: League Feint-Pattern Annotation
hotspots.description: The league tower-defense desk's annotation pinned to the tank as cross-reference, naming the third-minute formation feint apprentices have not been taught to wait out.

hotspots.name: Dean's Admission Recording
hotspots.description: On the curriculum-affairs board: the Dean's recorded admission. 'I knew Module 17 was absent. The apprentices were not the failures. The curriculum was.'

hotspots.name: Auro's Trade-Empire Employment Record
hotspots.description: Trade-Empire intelligence board: Auro on payroll as a 'route-safety contractor' for nine years — since Year 5, since the first apprentice failure.

hotspots.name: Dean's Full Admission
hotspots.description: Pinned beside Auro's record: the Dean's full admission of deferring to Tarn for fourteen years, with no excuse for the last six.

hotspots.name: Three-Amendment Council Options
hotspots.description: On the council-vote display: the three amendment options — restore named, restore anonymously, or refuse and fund Auro's Trade-Empire role permanently.

hotspots.name: Faculty Meeting Minutes — Week Before
hotspots.description: On the curriculum-affairs board: three faculty heads in violent disagreement, then a quiet hour, then unanimous agreement on 'Tarn must speak.' Tarn was not at the meeting.

hotspots.name: Trial Faculty Proposal — Roen
hotspots.description: Beside the minutes: five modules, ritual-heavy, citing Tarn's authority-trial framework. Signed by Roen. Proposes a celebration-trial co-requisite.

hotspots.name: Dean's Council-Brief Draft
hotspots.description: On the Council-brief board: ratify the curriculum and let Tarn go, or summon Tarn back and tell the Academy the truth about the vote. The brief is unsigned.

hotspots.name: Three Faculty Apologies
hotspots.description: On the rite-record board: Othmar, Veth, and the Dean each wrote a public apology. Roen has not — Roen kept Tarn's confidence and was the only one not in the wrong.

hotspots.name: Curriculum-Authorship Motion
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite ballot display: 'curriculum by Professor Tarn' or 'curriculum, anonymous.' Both motions ratify the same modules. The choice is the player's.

hotspots.name: Council Communiqué of the Six
hotspots.description: On the chronicle-public display: the Antiquarian's communiqué naming all six Watchers by band and audience, thanking the seventh for the silence — the Ark's first public statement on the founding Watchers in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Severance Roster — Two Hundred Sixteen Names
hotspots.description: On the Severance roster-board: two hundred sixteen names every season. The first three are the same three names in the same order, every season since Year 1.

hotspots.name: Vex's Three-Name Confirmation
hotspots.description: Pinned beside the roster: Vex confirms the three first names are the inheritor (different each year) and two fixed witnesses. 'That part is the bond's, not mine.'

hotspots.name: Klessa's Failsafe — Thirty-Nine Wax-Pours
hotspots.description: On the failsafe-role board: if a season passes without a successor, Klessa pours the candle wax across the bond's table-line. She has done this thirty-nine times.

hotspots.name: Written Protocol — Eleven Lines
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite display: eleven lines hand-copied from the apprentice oath, ratified by Vex Maestro and Auditor Klessa, witnessed by the Architect's Console.

hotspots.name: League Ledger-Keeper Wall
hotspots.description: The personnel display: forty seasons of ledger-keepers, forty handwriting samples, none matching the clause-writing hand. One anomaly — a Year-One name that does not appear on the wall.

hotspots.name: Zyr'Koth's Council-Chamber Arrival
hotspots.description: On the arrival log: the hall does not go silent. The hall goes quieter — the kind of quiet a room makes when it remembers a story it would rather not tell.

hotspots.name: Advocate's Six-Page Brief
hotspots.description: On the Council-brief board: every infernal clause cites a non-existent prize from the date of writing. Every clause is voidable as a matter of contract law. Includes Atalin's signed witness statement.

hotspots.name: Atalin's Council-Floor Apology
hotspots.description: On the Council-floor recording: Atalin apologises to the league for forty seasons of unease, and to the Hierarchy for the trap. The Hierarchy accepts in writing. The league does not need to.

hotspots.name: Council Vote — Amnesty Passed
hotspots.description: On the Council-vote display: twelve to two, three abstentions. Every infernal clause across forty seasons is declared void by the Council in session.

hotspots.name: Advocate's Closing Speech — Eleven Minutes
hotspots.description: On the closing-rite recording: 'we have been winning by honest paperwork. we will keep winning that way. it is not a glamorous habit, but it is a survivable one.'

hotspots.name: Four-House Delegation at the Council Door
hotspots.description: On the Council-chamber door log: four people in working clothes. Two old, two young. They will not give names until they have read theirs into the record.

hotspots.name: Foundation-Day Council Briefing Pack
hotspots.description: On the Council-briefing board: the Antiquarian's pack — everything except the name. The Council can ratify, amend, or contest. None of the three options name the seventh.

hotspots.name: Kassel's Council-Floor Speech
hotspots.description: On the Council-floor recording: 'we are asking the charter to admit it had eight names from the start. there is a difference, and the charter knows the difference.'

hotspots.name: Kassel's Silence-as-Vote Response
hotspots.description: Pinned beside: Kassel's recorded response. 'The schism is asking for the seventh's silence to be heard correctly, four epochs late.'

hotspots.name: Council Vote — Option Three Passes
hotspots.description: On the Council-vote display: eleven votes to four, with two abstentions. Two of the four nay-voters apologise from the floor.

hotspots.name: Three-Option Council Ballot
hotspots.description: Beside the ratification: (1) ratify the schism, (2) close the schism, (3) ratify backward AND keep the original intact. Drafted by the player and the Antiquarian.

hotspots.name: Plaza-Audience Watcher-Line Tallies
hotspots.description: On the plaza-audience board: three players confirm Idris's voice; two confirm Verel's; five remain unconfirmed. The unconfirmed five are the four other named Watchers' work, plus the seventh's silence.

hotspots.name: Player's First Question — Year-Vault Draft
hotspots.description: On the year-vault-archive board: the player's hand-written first question for the silent seventh, sealed in an envelope to be opened next Memorial Day.

hotspots.name: Thaloria Battle Logs — Akai Shi's Last Hours
hotspots.description: On the Thaloria archive board: energy-manipulation discharges, healing applied to seven Potentials, then 'subject consumed' at hour four. Jericho intercepted at hour seven.

hotspots.name: Empire of Shadows — Current Status
hotspots.description: On the Empire-status board: the charter holds. The bindings on all ten named demon lords are operationally intact. The Advocate has not retired the charter.

hotspots.name: Hierarchy Acquisition-Attempt Log
hotspots.description: On the defensive display: seven centuries of Hierarchy attempts against Advocate-sheltered souls. Every outcome where the countersignature held: NULL.

hotspots.name: Riri'Ahlia's Siege Account
hotspots.description: Pinned beside the log: the Hierarchy COO's surviving account of the seven-dimensions siege. 'The Advocate had MORE only in one resource: she was willing to spend herself.' A retreat at a moment her instruments could still have continued.

hotspots.name: Advocate's Blood-Weave Journals
hotspots.description: On the Empire-of-Shadows display: the Advocate's operational journals — every Weave deployment within a Storm-active window, the Storm credited as 'a patron of opportunity, indifferent to outcome.'

hotspots.name: Calm-Event Correlation Table
hotspots.description: The war-room's correlation table mapping the Storm's nine calms onto the chronicle's most consequential planning events. Seven matched; two unrecorded; the chronicle's gap, not the cadence's.

hotspots.name: Second Fall Casualty Count
hotspots.description: On the New-Babylon-affairs board: the Second Fall's casualty count. Millions among the populace; zero among Potentials; zero among awake Ne-Yons. The cult calls it miraculous; the Architect did not intervene.

hotspots.name: Ocularum Vigil Board
hotspots.description: A standing-threat panel on the tactical archive's lower rack — institutional powers the room tracks without engaging. The Authority's six minds head the list.

hotspots.name: Ocularum Cell Roster
hotspots.description: A roster card in the archive's deepest drawer — the Ocularum's modern register. Three named cells of seven hundred.

hotspots.name: Hierarchy Org-Chart Board
hotspots.description: A captured-document panel on the tactical archive's upper rack — the Hierarchy's internal Severance project org chart. One reporting line, one apex.

hotspots.name: Thalorian Defence Records
hotspots.description: A defence-doctrine binder in the comparative-history drawer — Thaloria's nine-generation consensual relaxation of its own recertification standards.

hotspots.name: New Babylon Siege Record
hotspots.description: A campaign binder in the siege-history drawer — Iron Lion's legions at New Babylon, Day 10 of Veil. The record is complete on her forces and silent on her death.

hotspots.name: Hierarchy Piece-Positioning Board
hotspots.description: A captured-document panel on the archive's deep rack — the Hierarchy of the Damned's aeons-long piece-positioning, read the way a war-room reads a slow board.

hotspots.name: Varkul Director-of-Security File
hotspots.description: A personnel order on the command-structure rack — Mol'Garath's post-Severance promotion of the Necromancer's creation to keeper of the Hierarchy's gates, both sides.

hotspots.name: Necromancer Castle-Log Board
hotspots.description: A captured Hierarchy R&D log on the document rack — the Castle of Death named in the standing tense from the CFO's office, and Riri'Ahlia's unanswered procedural question.

hotspots.name: Zyr'Koth R&D Refinement File
hotspots.description: Captured Hierarchy R&D working notes on the document rack — the Advocate's defensive Weave inverted into the Severance, the source technique cited before the change, the test cohort redacted.

hotspots.name: The Severance Hollowing Report
hotspots.description: A Hierarchy R&D observation note on a redacted test subject — a casualty with no wound — and Zyr'Koth's filed no-position on whether the protocol is ever used.

hotspots.name: The Locked-Lever Board
hotspots.description: A strategic-assessment panel — the Severance as the only tested reversal of a Syl'Vex conversion, held only by a clause in Mol'Garath's quarterly review.

hotspots.name: The Dual-Roster Board
hotspots.description: Two roster entries for one operative pinned side by side — Mira Halen 'in good standing' on the Insurgency's roster and 'Convert. Recognized.' on the Hierarchy's, both current, neither forged — and the cost-audit that came back blank.

hotspots.name: The Severance Cross-Lock File
hotspots.description: The Severance design read against a Syl'Vex convert — extracts one thread, never deployed on a convert — and Mol'Garath's quarterly-review clause requiring a consent never sought.

hotspots.name: The Taskmaster's Siege Portfolio
hotspots.description: A captured Hierarchy operations file on the document rack — the siege of seven dimensions filed not as a campaign but as a portfolio entry with a populated remediation field, and the Taskmaster's own status-grammar register.

hotspots.name: The Reorganization-Doctrine Board
hotspots.description: A strategic-assessment panel — Riri'Ahlia's doctrine of reorganizing value off a position she cannot take, her silence as her most active state, and Fenra's post-siege seventeen-dimension commendation.

hotspots.name: The Procedural-Question File
hotspots.description: A captured Hierarchy procedural filing cross-referenced against the necromancer-castle log — Riri'Ahlia's canonically unanswered question filed to be on the record, and the doctrine that the record is the org chart's edge.

hotspots.name: The Priced-Defense Accounting
hotspots.description: Riri'Ahlia's own filed after-action ledger of the siege — expenditure within projection, the assault vector retired, and the one line that mattered: the cost of the Advocate's defense, now measured and in the portfolio.

hotspots.name: The Seventeen-Front Manifest
hotspots.description: Fenra's captured operational record, racked beside the Taskmaster's siege portfolio — the seventeen-dimension invasion filed as a supply manifest, fed from one kitchen, the berserker read struck as the false lead.

hotspots.name: The Wolf-in-the-Boardroom File
hotspots.description: A captured Hierarchy personnel portrait — the fur-lined coat and the lupine snout filed as one canon, the growl that lands on the bookkeeping not the kill, and the silence that is restraint, not the Taskmaster's reorganization or Varkul's vigil.

hotspots.name: The Fenra-Varkul Contrast Record
hotspots.description: Filed beside the Varkul director-of-security order — the Necromancer's two senior creations read as a matched pair: the still door and the moving engine, the two things any continuity needs.

hotspots.name: Holo Table Dial
hotspots.description: The brass dial at the holo-table's edge. BRIEFING / RECON / OBITUARY. Currently set to BRIEFING.

hotspots.name: Casualty Board
hotspots.description: Oxblood-leather binders racked along the left wall, each labelled with an operation name and a year. The thickest is PROTOCOL ZERO.

hotspots.name: Signal Flag Rack
hotspots.description: Stage-left rack of folded signal-flags between the bookshelf and the war-table. Twelve flags, one per faction Lyra negotiated with in person.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Live Signature Sample
hotspots.description: On the signature-comparison bench: Per. M.'s receipt from this morning, laid under the lens beside the preservation-order file. The doubled-pulse tic matches the wax-thumb on the seventh signature.

hotspots.name: Founding-Watcher Oath, Stanza Three
hotspots.description: A brittle vellum scrap recovered from the cipher-den's deepest archive — older than the charter. Three lines name the closer's role and the oath that keeps it silent.

hotspots.name: Roen's Confidential Account
hotspots.description: In the cipher-den's closed wing: Trial-master Roen's full statement on the three-month-old conversation in which Tarn asked them for help leaving without a goodbye.

hotspots.name: Cross-Reference: Five Recovered
hotspots.description: On the cross-reference bench: the first-pass results — five names recovered by listening to the unwitnessed imprints in pairs. The chain of memory was not broken at every link.

hotspots.name: Parental Imprint Search
hotspots.description: Beside the first-pass bench: the expanded search across the wider registry. Two hits — a parent imprinted in epoch four named I-244; a sibling imprinted in epoch six named I-44.

hotspots.name: The First-Imprint Record
hotspots.description: From the pre-charter tier: the record of the Ark's first imprint. 'Witnessing I-1.' Taken before the founding charter, by the Architect's own first act.

hotspots.name: Heron's Diary
hotspots.description: Drawer eleven, fourth-epoch tier — the Council archivist Heron's personal diary, recovered from a sealed compartment in their desk. A confession written in advance of the confessor's pardon.

hotspots.name: Heron's Diary, Page Two
hotspots.description: The diary's second page: Heron asking the seventh whether they consented to the scrub, and recording the silence both Heron and the Council misread.

hotspots.name: Silence-as-Vote Convention
hotspots.description: The founding-protocols archive's page on the convention Heron did not honour. The seventh Watcher has been voting no by silence since the fourth epoch, exactly as the convention prescribes.

hotspots.name: Forty-Contract Handwriting Analysis
hotspots.description: On the signature-comparison bench: the cipher-den's report — forty clauses, one writer, consistent across forty seasons, no match to any seasonal ledger-keeper.

hotspots.name: Atalin's Receipt — Bench Match
hotspots.description: Pulled from Atalin's archived personnel file: a routine receipt whose hand matches the clause-writing exactly. The cipher-den's annotation: 'identity confirmed.'

hotspots.name: The Trap Atalin Wrote In
hotspots.description: In the annotated-contract drawer: every clause names 'the second-cycle prize.' The league didn't institute second-cycle prizes until season eleven. Forty clauses, every one voidable.

hotspots.name: Tarn's Year-One Argument
hotspots.description: Drawer seven, year-one tier — the recovered audio of Tarn's forty-minute Year-One argument against Module 17, bookmarked at hour three.

hotspots.name: Seven-Day Window — Exact Dates
hotspots.description: On the window-precision bench: epoch one, week thirty-three, days four through ten. The writer worked retroactively for the first contract, prospectively for the others.

hotspots.name: Eighth Sigil — Hand Opening, Two Fingers Down
hotspots.description: On the sigil-reference bench: the eighth sigil from the mirror charter. Last appeared in lower-deck tax ledgers four epochs ago.

hotspots.name: Scrub-Pattern Handwriting Cross-Reference
hotspots.description: On the handwriting-cross-reference bench: the redaction's hand matches three other epoch-four scrubs across unrelated archives — all removing artisan-house references. One systematic person.

hotspots.name: Per. M.'s Doubled-Pulse Signature Tic
hotspots.description: On the signature-rhythm bench: a doubled pulse in every Per. M. signature — a tic present in writers who breathe twice per stroke. Documented in founding-Watcher physiology.

hotspots.name: Candle Smoke Residue Across Ledgers
hotspots.description: On the chemical-trace bench: Klessa's candle leaves the same residue on every Severance ledger. The mark predates Klessa, predates the league, matches the Broker's shelf candles.

hotspots.name: Broker's First Name — Year-One Residue Match
hotspots.description: On the residue-match bench at case-closure: the Broker is named Solène. They redacted themselves at the first ceremony so the role would not become a person.

hotspots.name: I-1 Relatives Search — No Result
hotspots.description: On the relatives-search bench: no parent imprinted, no sibling imprinted, no witnesses recorded. I-1 is alone in the registry.

hotspots.name: Logic Faculty Proposal — Othmar
hotspots.description: On the faculty-submissions bench: eight modules, chess-heavy, citing Tarn's residency notes. Signed by Othmar. Proposes elimination of two trial-faculty modules.

hotspots.name: Verel's Band-Five Signature
hotspots.description: On the spectrum-analysis bench: band-five card. Bright waveform, narrow spectrum, an overtone like running water. Verel speaks to caretakers.

hotspots.name: Syndicate Seven-Pointed Star Footer
hotspots.description: On the Syndicate-of-Death roster bench: six twin-pairs, six bindings, the canonical six-pointed star embossed on every page. The Resurrectionist's case-file footer carries a seven-pointed star, drawn with the same precision.

hotspots.name: Targets-List — Order Pattern Analysis
hotspots.description: On the pattern-analysis bench: the targets sorted by how much each elimination redirected the chronicle. Ascending. The Red Death is building toward something.

hotspots.name: Crucible Seal Telemetry — Wolf's Chamber
hotspots.description: On the containment-telemetry bench: the Wolf's seal at 92% at transfer, failed 23 cycles later. Anara's containment ledger does not register the Wolf's chamber as a chamber.

hotspots.name: Storm — Uncorrelated Calm Residue
hotspots.description: On the pattern-anomaly bench: two of nine calms have no recorded chronicle-event. The cult annotates them 'atmospheric'; the signatures are identical to the seven correlated calms.

hotspots.name: Year-One Curriculum-Vote Full Proceedings
hotspots.description: On the year-one-audio bench: six and a half hours of recovered audio. Hour three is the curriculum debate; Tarn's forty-minute argument against Module 17 sits inside it.

hotspots.name: Upper-Band Signature Cards
hotspots.description: On the spectrum-analysis bench: six distinct upper-band signatures from the silence-break, and a seventh signature present-and-silent throughout the sixty-three-second event.

hotspots.name: Idris's Band-Three Signature
hotspots.description: Beside the bench: the band-three card isolated. Slow waveform, standing-silence undercurrent. Matches the registry placeholder the cipher-den has held for eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Six-Watcher Master Catalogue
hotspots.description: On the master catalogue: six cards arranged by band — Idris, Verel, Ophran, Kallium, Mereth, Sothe. The first complete cipher-den entry for the upper-bands Watchers in eight epochs.

hotspots.name: Necromancer's Matrix Retreat Chambers
hotspots.description: On the matrix-cartography bench: a schematic of the Necromancer's seven retreat chambers — defense-in-depth designed for chronicle-space hunters. The Red Death is not one.

hotspots.name: Surveillance Network
hotspots.description: The four large green monitor screens flanking the chamber (2 on each side wall) — live feeds from across the Ark and beyond.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Enigma's surveillance network. It doesn't just monitor the Ark — it taps into communication channels across multiple realities. Those feeds show conversations happening right now in the Panopticon, the Terminus Hive, even the Antiquarian's Library. The Enigma saw everything. Knew everything. And trusted no one.

hotspots.name: Conspiracy Boards
hotspots.description: The three framed silhouette portraits in the center-back — Lyra, Wraith, and Vox. String-and-photo evidence connecting events across the entire Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The conspiracy boards. Every thread connects to every other thread. The Architect's true identity. The Oracle's hidden agenda. The Collector's real purpose. The Enigma mapped it all. Some of these connections are terrifying — they suggest that certain events in the Saga weren't accidents. They were orchestrated by someone operating above even the Architect's awareness.

hotspots.name: Return to Comms Array
hotspots.description: The hidden panel back to the main Communications Array — walk out through the foreground.

hotspots.name: Master Cipher Key
hotspots.description: A small device that can decrypt any message in the Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Master Cipher Key. The Enigma's ultimate tool. It can decrypt any message, crack any code, bypass any encryption in the entire Dischordian Saga. With this, there are no more secrets. The Enigma left it here with a note: 'The truth will set you free. But first, it will make you very, very angry.' Use it wisely, Spy.

hotspots.name: Rosetta Pad
hotspots.description: A thick brass-bound codex on a reading-stand at the centre of the desk. Three columns: indigo glyphs, Elara's warm-gold, and a third hand in old black ink — Lyra Vox's translation key.

hotspots.name: Encrypted Correspondence
hotspots.description: Cubbyholes along the back wall stuffed with rolled letters — Lyra and Wraith's cipher exchange in the last six months of her command.

hotspots.name: Dictionary of Edits
hotspots.description: A freestanding lectern stage-left with a perpetually-open book. Pages turn themselves at one every fifteen seconds — the editor's vocabulary catalogued.

hotspots.name: Uncorruption Bench
hotspots.description: A worktop stage-right with a brass-rimmed magnifier on a swing-arm. Combine corrupted-fragments here with their originals — the lens does the work.

hotspots.name: Cross-Arc Thanks Card
hotspots.description: A small index card in a brass frame on the cross-arc shelf — Velkraal's final-edit gratitude state, updating with the player's choices.

hotspots.name: Vex-Seer Pair Binder
hotspots.description: A two-pocket binder on the Insurgency-engineer shelf — the Seer's consultation request to Vex and a state-card mirroring his undelivered letter.

hotspots.name: Judges' Bench
hotspots.description: The long brass-and-oak slab elevated on three steps at chamber-back, three high-backed chairs with amber lamps flanking. The chief adjudicator's middle seat is taller by a hand's-width.

hotspots.name: Scale of Justice
hotspots.description: The golden scales-of-justice motif inlaid on the foreground floor — weighs not gold or silver but intention and consequence.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Scale of Justice. It weighs not gold or silver, but intention and consequence. Every major decision in the Saga was evaluated by this scale. The Hierophant used it to determine which actions served the greater good and which served only selfish desire. It's responding to your presence — it recognizes a champion of Order.

hotspots.name: Law Archives
hotspots.description: The left-wall audience pillars with purple-glyph strip lighting — holographic tomes containing every law and code of the Saga.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The complete legal code of the Dischordian Saga. Laws governing reality itself — the Conservation of Narrative Energy, the Prohibition of Temporal Paradox, the Right of Every Potential to Choose Their Own Path. The Hierophant wrote most of these. Some say they're the only thing preventing the multiverse from collapsing into chaos.

hotspots.name: Evidence Locker
hotspots.description: The right-wall jury box with chairs — a wall of small brass-faced compartments behind. Most empty. Three sealed in red wax — open cases, awaiting verdict.

hotspots.name: Return to Bridge
hotspots.description: The formal corridor back to the Command Bridge.

hotspots.name: Apprentice Rostrum
hotspots.description: The left-side audience rostrum — the Mechronis Academy trial cadence; mentor a successor through the 28-day trial.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Mechronis trial rostrum. You mentor a successor through the twelve-archetype, twenty-eight-day trial — while the Politician's dead insurance policy trains your rival's. The loop is a mirror.

hotspots.name: Mol'Vereth's Audit Ledger
hotspots.description: A small bound volume on a side-shelf beside the judges' bench — Mol'Vereth files every annual audit through this ledger.

hotspots.name: Judge's Audit Trail — Lycos Open Entry
hotspots.description: On the judges' bench front (left lamp area): the Judge's open entry under Day 15 of Resonance, Year 100,001 A.A. 'The work was clean. The instrument was not lost.'

hotspots.name: The Judge's Audit Clarification
hotspots.description: On the judges' bench front (center): the Second Ne-Yon's terse reply, distinguishing the instrument He destroyed (the Thought Virus) from the instrument that was preserved (Lycos).

hotspots.name: Judge's Storm-Silence Arbitration Register
hotspots.description: On the judges' bench front (right lamp area): seven Judge-arbitrations between the Storm and the Silence, each closed with the same standing position — 'keep the polarity.'

hotspots.name: Reality Forges
hotspots.description: Three cauldrons burn with flames of different colors — yellow probability, red paradox, cyan déjà vu — each warping reality around it.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The Reality Forges. Each one burns a different fuel — compressed probability, crystallized paradox, liquefied déjà vu. The Meme used them to forge weapons that shouldn't exist. A sword that cuts through time. A shield that reflects consequences. A bomb that erases the concept of a specific idea. Chaos isn't destruction — it's unlimited creativity.

hotspots.name: Chaos Equations
hotspots.description: The back wall behind the central red cauldron — brilliant equations scrawled alongside anarchist graffiti.
hotspots.elaraDialog: The equations of chaos. They look like madness, but each one solves an impossible problem. How to travel faster than light without a ship. How to exist in two places simultaneously. How to make a joke so funny it literally rewrites reality. The Meme was a genius — they just expressed their genius through destruction and humor rather than order and logic.

hotspots.name: Return to Engineering Bay
hotspots.description: A keyhole-vault door on the far-right wall leading back to Engineering.

hotspots.name: Chaos Anvil
hotspots.description: The central anvil pedestal at chamber center — asymmetric, heavier on the left than the right. Strikes ring different harmonics depending on where they land.

hotspots.name: Entropy Vat
hotspots.description: The left-most cauldron with yellow flames — a copper-rimmed bath of seething oil that never settles. Used for tempering — and, by deliberate design, for refusing the smith their certainty.

hotspots.name: Convergence Point
hotspots.description: The central flame on a tall pedestal between the four pillars — where fire, water, earth, and air merge into pure white energy.
